IT DID NOT MATTER.' Casualties also subtract inside the score (-1 per 100,000 own dead per era, floor -10) so that even a settled conventional war costs points. A SCARRED era is printed in the paper with a black rule and the word in the masthead strip so the player never learns the cap at 1970.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The ledger gap as the trailing side's risk appetite (the runaway effect without an auto-win)
mechanics_recommendations.why: TS's 20-VP threshold and Pax Pamir's early-end rule make a lead a threat that forces the loser into desperate, DEFCON-risky play. UGS wants that pressure to arrive as escalation, not as an end screen: the losing pole should court the brink, which is pillar 1 doing what the elevator pitch says.
mechanics_recommendations.how: At each monthly AI allocator pass, read gap = (rival's provisional era score - own) for USA/SOV. Feed it as one signed integer into (a) the coup-launch threshold once AI coups arrive in v1.5 (a trailing Moscow launches at CHANCES ABOUT EVEN, a leading one waits for PROBABLE), and (b) the crisis escalate-vs-back-down weight (trailing side climbs one rung further before backing down). Print it: the rival's chequebook line in the paper gains the cause word ('MOSCOW ACTIVE — BEHIND ON THE LEDGER'). Deterministic because it reads a monthly integer; cheap because it is a single term in existing decisions; and it gives the leading player a reason to fear a large lead, which is the 'win without ending the world' tension in one rule.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The Chinese Civil War handicap, translated: a starting-par bid for multiplayer and for 'hard' single-player
mechanics_recommendations.why: TS tournaments balance sides with an influence bid rather than a rules change; UGS's difficulty setting for the same reason should move the par, not the formula, so every difficulty and every nation is scored by the same arithmetic and the harness stays meaningful.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Scenario setup exposes one integer `par_bid` per pole (default 0): it is added to the 1950 par of that pole's MAP term. Playing the USSR on 'historical' difficulty is par_bid 0 (the hands-off world is already East +16 on the map); 'hard' for the USA is par_bid -6 (you must hold more than history held); lockstep multiplayer bids for sides exactly as WBC does. Nothing else in the sim changes, and the paper prints the bid on the founding edition ('THE WEST STARTS THE DECADE SIX POINTS IN CREDIT').

pitfalls: Scoring the board absolutely: the contestable battleground set is structurally Western (every Soviet holding is locked and off-set), so TS values give West +41 in 1950 and +28 hands-off in 1965 — a permanent blowout that makes the USSR's game 'lose more slowly'. Score deltas from a 1950 par (TS's zero-marker) and the same run reads East +13 on the map, which is the historical story.

Integrating monthly (Through the Ages culture) instead of snapshotting: an asymmetric opening multiplied by 240 months drowns every decision; snapshot deltas at four dates keep the identity 'sum of eras = board since 1950'.

Putting Armageddon or great-power casualties into the score as points: a leader will price them. The catastrophe state must be lexicographically above the score with grade caps, and GameOver must print the frozen ledger as an epitaph rather than suppress it.

The settlement loophole: ClientState and Neutralization clauses write alignment at the patron's edge and lock it, so a conventional WW3 won by imposed peace paints the map and scores. Do not close the loophole in the map term (that is the influence pillar working as designed); close it with the SCARRED cap, the casualty debit and the annexation tension floor, so the war is playable but capped at COSTLY.
Double counting: printing the absolute board AND summing it with era deltas rewards the 1950 lead twice. Print the board as context only; sum only the era ledgers.

Reading REPORTED industry for a planned economy's OUTPUT term: the planner's dashboard lies by design (falsified fulfilment reports). The reckoning must read actual_centi and print the gap — that is the epistemic drama, not a bug.

Letting the AI allocator or the timeline see the checkpoint date: the AI must be checkpoint-blind (it is today) so the pre-freeze rush is a player behaviour bounded by flow rates, not a scripted panic; and no event may carry a 'scores +N' effect — the map, legitimacy and output are the only score inputs.

Tuning the MAP term to make hands-off land where you want it: the map term is the influence pillar's calibration harness target; the OUTPUT cap and STANDING bands are the only score knobs. Add a hands_off_verdict diagnostic that prints the four era ledgers and asserts the campaign band, or the verdict will drift as the timeline corpus grows.

Building a bespoke non-aligned victory (QMG: The Cold War's third faction): score the field through the existing denied column with the same verdict function; India, Egypt and Yugoslavia score 'does the field hold my region', not a new formula.
Percentages and raw permille on the reckoning page: every term is a small signed integer with a cause phrase and a grade word; the Kent legend stays in the politics panel footer.

The unused `weight` field: battleground weights (1-3) drive the AI allocator but not standings. Either keep TS's flat +1 per battleground in the score (recommended: totals stay in the TS range where the region values were calibrated) or document that weight is priority, not value — do not silently switch to weighted counts, which triples the totals and breaks the value table.
analysts.first_hour_test: On the paused 1950-01-01 screen the founding edition of the paper carries THE LEDGER box: 'PAR SET 1 JANUARY 1950. THE FIRST RECKONING: 1 JANUARY 1955 (60 MONTHS).' followed by the six regional verdict words for both poles exactly as the standings already compute them (EUROPE: WEST DOMINATES; THE AMERICAS: WEST CONTROLS CENTRAL AMERICA, DOMINATES THE SOUTH; ASIA, MIDDLE EAST: WEST PRESENT; AFRICA: NO ONE), the OUTPUT line with the player's own figure exact and the rival's as an estimate ('INDUSTRY PER HEAD: OURS 100, THEIRS EST. 35-55'), STANDING ('LEGITIMACY: NEUTRAL'), CATASTROPHE ('UNSCARRED'), and the provisional verdict sentence 'IF THE RECKONING WERE TODAY: STALEMATE — NOTHING HAS MOVED SINCE THE PAR.' A HUD chip reads 'RECKONING IN 60 MO'. Across January-June 1950 the player sees two sourced elections on the wire (Britain 23 Feb, Greece 5 Mar) with no band change, the UNSC 83 legitimacy grant in late June lifting the American STANDING line to +3 ('IF TODAY: WEST +3, NARROW — ON LEGITIMACY ALONE'), and, if they placed an aid or presence program, the target's dossier PRESSURES ledger showing the flow but the provisional map line still reading 0, because no battleground can cross 300 in six months at tier 1 — the ledger teaches that the map is slow and the reckoning is far. At the 1955 checkpoint, hands off, THE RECKONING page prints: MAP 0 (the board is the par: West 41, East 0 under the region values), OUTPUT +3 or +4 West, STANDING +3 West (UNSC 83), CATASTROPHE UNSCARRED for both poles (Korea settled without nuclear use and under a million American dead), grade NARROW WESTERN, sentence 'THE 1955 RECKONING: NARROW WESTERN LEAD. THE MAP HAS NOT MOVED; THE WEST LEADS ON OUTPUT AND STANDING. THE FIELD HOLDS ASIA AND THE MIDDLE EAST.' — and the East's chequebook line naming the three presence programs Moscow is running in India, Indonesia and Yugoslavia, so the player who is Washington knows where the next era will be lost and the player who is Moscow knows where to win it.

findings.title: Every score display that works in the genre is a ranked word, not a number; every one that fails is a sum shown live
findings.detail: Civilization VI's World Rankings (2016; 'Victory Progress' tabs) are the strongest 4X precedent because each tab is a ranked list per VICTORY TYPE with a 'who is closest and how far' line ('Gandhi: 3 of 8 civilizations converted'), while its Score tab — the sum — is the one nobody reads and Score Victory is the ending players disable. Civ V's Demographics screen is the model for a per-column readout: category | yours | rank | best | average | worst, with no total. EU4's ledger (2013) has a top-bar Score (ADM+DIP+MIL) that is universally ignored, but its Great Power rank (1.26, 2016) and Age Objectives (1.20 Mandate of Heaven, 2017 — checkbox goals per age) are legible because they are a RANK and a LIST. Victoria 2's rank is the best Paradox case: Great Power = a sum of three NAMED sub-ranks (prestige/industry/military), so a player can say 'I am #6 because my industry rank is 11'. Victoria 3 (2022) regressed: prestige is a decimal that updates continuously and decomposes only in a hover tooltip ('prestige from goods produced'), which produced the recurring 2022-23 Paradox-forum complaint that prestige is gamed by building arms and ships rather than read; its Objectives (Economic Dominance / Hegemony / Egalitarian Society) are checklists that most players forget exist because they are not tied to a periodic reckoning. HoI4 has no scoreboard at all and its most common endgame complaint is 'when do I stop?'. Lesson for UGS: print a rank/verdict word per named column, never a total, and never anything that changes faster than the monthly paper.
findings.evidence: Civilization VI World Rankings screen (Firaxis, 2016); Civilization V Demographics screen (2010); EU4 ledger and Score (Paradox 1.0, 2013), Great Power rank (1.26 'Rights of Man', 2016), Age Objectives (1.20, 2017); Victoria 2 rank formula (2010); Victoria 3 prestige tooltip and Objectives (1.0, Oct 2022); Paradox forum threads on Vic3 prestige-from-goods 2022-23; Soren Johnson, 'Playing to Lose' / 'players will optimize the fun out of a game' (Game Developer column, 2011).

findings.title: Twilight Struggle's VP track is legible because every VP has a printed cause, and the Reckoning should copy the scoring card, not the track
findings.detail: Twilight Struggle (GMT 2005, Gupta & Matthews) uses one shared 20-point track, and it is readable not because it is a number but because every movement comes from a card whose text states the cause ('+1 VP per battleground'), and because regional scoring cards force a periodic Presence/Domination/Control reckoning that UGS has already adopted. What does not transfer: the track is exact, symmetric and two-player. What transfers exactly: (1) a scoring EVENT at a known moment, printed as a table of regions with the verdict word per side; (2) the DEFCON-1 rule — the player who caused it LOSES, everyone else does not win — which is the right attribution for a general exchange; (3) the rulebook publishes the scoring formula so players plan toward it. Balance of Power (Chris Crawford, 1985) is the elevator pitch's direct ancestor and shows the danger: its single 'geopolitical prestige' number was legible only because there were two players, and its nuclear-war screen ('We do not reward failure') — already quoted in crates/ugs-app/src/endgame.rs:142 — is the correct tone for the catastrophe epilogue: no score at all.
findings.evidence: Twilight Struggle rulebook (GMT, deluxe ed. 2009) sections on Scoring Cards and DEFCON; Balance of Power (Mindscape, 1985) manual and end screen; docs/design/systems/influence.md 'The score' section; crates/ugs-app/src/endgame.rs lines 72-142.

findings.title: Suzerain and Frostpunk prove an epilogue is legible only when each line names the decision that caused it
findings.detail: Suzerain (Torpor Games, 2020) ends with a slide-based text epilogue, one slide per character/institution, with no numbers; players rate it highly because every slide is attributable ('Because you signed the ... , the ...'). Its weakness is the mirror image: during play the only standing surface is the in-game newspaper and the ministers' reports, and players routinely reach the epilogue not knowing they had been losing — the reckoning must therefore appear DURING the campaign too, in the same voice. Frostpunk (11 bit, 2018) closes with one sentence of judgment ('The city survived.') and an optional moral rider ('But was it worth it?') whenever a line was crossed; that rider is exactly how a 'won' nuclear exchange should read. Crusader Kings 3's 'Legacy' score screen is the counter-example: a total and a chart, no causes, ignored. The UGS epilogue therefore is: one verdict sentence, then THE THREE THINGS THAT DECIDED IT, each a dated, templated line pointing at a checkpoint row or a fired event ('AFRICA WENT EAST AT THE 1960 RECKONING (4 OF 7 BATTLEGROUNDS)'), then the ledger of four columns as words. Never a bar chart of score over time.
findings.evidence: Suzerain epilogue and 'The Sordland Herald' newspaper (Torpor Games, 2020); Frostpunk ending sequence (11 bit studios, 2018); Crusader Kings 3 end-of-game Legacy screen (Paradox, 2020).

findings.title: The house template already exists: the war room's ASSESSMENT sentence is the standing verdict with the nouns swapped
findings.detail: crates/ugs-app/src/war_ui.rs lines 1527-1539 compute the dominant momentum term and template 'ASSESSMENT: YOU ARE LOSING -- CASUALTY EXCHANGE RUNS AGAINST YOU'. The economic-agency readup's principle 2 ('print the argmin as a verdict sentence') and the war-legibility readup's principle 3 ('largest modifier gap, template a sentence, ~50 lines') both converge on the same shape. The standing verdict is the same 50 lines over four signed columns: word = LEADING / EVEN / TRAILING from the sign and margin of the total; cause = the column with the largest negative (or, when leading, positive) contribution; pointer = the panel key that owns that column ('[P] POLITICS'). Printed as 'OUR STANDING: TRAILING -- ASIA RUNS AGAINST US [P]'. Because the words come from the monthly standings and the monthly RegionSnapshots, the sentence can only change at month rollover, which is the anti-score-watching guarantee for free.
findings.evidence: crates/ugs-app/src/war_ui.rs:1527-1543; docs/research/economic-agency.md principle 2; docs/research/war-legibility.md principle 3; docs/design/systems/newspaper.md 'THE WORLD IN NUMBERS'.

findings.title: Uncertainty must be stated in the rival column, and the rival's OWN claim is a third, separate line that the sim already knows how to fabricate
findings.detail: The paper is 'the world as you believe it'. So the Reckoning table has three columns per term: OURS (exact — own losses/figures are always exact, war-legibility principle 5), THEIR ESTIMATE (a two-significant-figure bracket through political/economic penetration, AS-OF stamped, Kent word when it is a standing: 'PROBABLY DOMINANT'), and AS THEY CLAIM (the rival's published figure). The claim line is cheap: the planned economy already carries dashboard_industry_centi (reported vs actual) and the paper masthead already picks the party organ for Eastern players — so 'PRAVDA CLAIMS: PLAN FULFILLED 108%, SOCIALIST CAMP LEADS IN ASIA' is rendered from the rival's REPORTED numbers, and the gap between claim and estimate is itself an intelligence finding the player learns to read. Historical warrant: Moscow published no statistical yearbook from 1947 until Narodnoe khozyaistvo SSSR v 1955 godu (1956), so Western standing estimates were RAND/CIA reconstructions (Bergson's Soviet GNP series), and the NIE 11-8 series (1958-61) overestimated Soviet missiles into the 'missile gap' — estimates are period flavor, and can be wrong. Rule: if the verdict word depends on an estimate wider than the margin, the word is qualified ('PROBABLY LEADING'), never flipped silently. At zero coverage the column prints '?' and the words 'MOSCOW DOES NOT PUBLISH'.
findings.evidence: docs/research/war-legibility.md principle 5 (HoI4 intel tiers, War in the Pacific claimed-vs-confirmed); Sherman Kent, 'Words of Estimative Probability', Studies in Intelligence 8:4 (1964); Narodnoe khozyaistvo SSSR (TsSU, first postwar yearbook 1956); Abram Bergson, 'The Real National Income of Soviet Russia since 1928' (Harvard/RAND, 1961); NIE 11-8-59 and successors on Soviet ICBM strength; crates/ugs-app/src/paper_ui.rs masthead and reported-figure handling.

findings.title: One scoring system fits 86 nations only if the comparator is data, not the rival: ship a historical PAR table
findings.detail: LEADING against whom? For the USA and USSR the rival is obvious; Egypt, Yugoslavia and Luxembourg have no rival, and a rank among 86 nations by score is the EU4-ledger anti-pattern (a minor is always #40 and learns nothing). The legible, deterministic, cheap comparator is PAR: the four column values every nation posts at each checkpoint in the hands-off run, which the project already computes (the hands_off_anchors_land_near_history and the_world_turns_to_1970 harnesses). Bake them into assets/data/scenario/1950/par.ron once per scenario build. Then every nation's verdict word is 'vs the record': Egypt 1960 'AHEAD OF HISTORY -- THE CANAL IS OURS AND THE TREASURY HOLDS'; bloc leaders get the head-to-head as a second line ('AND LEADING MOSCOW'). This also gives the founding edition a legible target on day one ('THE RECORD SAYS: EUROPE HOLDS, ASIA IS LOST BY 1955') and gives the epilogue its verdict vocabulary — BEAT THE CENTURY / HELD THE LINE / LOST THE DECADE — in golf-like terms that read the same for a superpower and a minor.
findings.evidence: docs/design/systems/influence.md 'Calibration' (hands_off_anchors_land_near_history, 40 anchors at 1955/1960/1965); docs/design/systems/world-timeline.md line 156 (the_world_turns_to_1970); EU4 ledger country-rank anti-pattern; Civ V Demographics 'average' column as the par idea in miniature.

findings.title: What NOT to show, with the reason each item breaks a house rule
findings.detail: (1) A live score number anywhere on the HUD or in a tooltip — any number that moves per tick is 'watching a simulation' (economic-agency principle 7) and any decimal invites optimising the fun out. (2) A score-over-time chart — CK3 Legacy / EU4 score graph: pretty, causeless. (3) An 86-row ranking table — minors read as losers; the paper prints only YOU, THE RIVAL (estimated), and the top MOVERS. (4) The rival's exact numbers — breaks epistemic texture; brackets and Kent words only. (5) Weights and permille in the UI — publish the rule once (the founding edition's HOW THE CENTURY IS SCORED box, in words, as Twilight Struggle's rulebook does), and keep the integer weights in a tuning module. (6) A live checkpoint countdown in hours — 'NEXT RECKONING: JAN 1955 (54 MONTHS)' in the paper only. (7) A 'you win' on the catastrophe screen under any circumstance; the exchange epilogue has its own vocabulary (RUIN) and prints the initiator, never a ranking. (8) Trend arrows that flip monthly on noise — an arrow requires two consecutive months in the same direction.
findings.evidence: docs/research/economic-agency.md principles 6-7; docs/research/war-legibility.md principle 5 (two significant figures, sample fuzz once per period); Twilight Struggle published scoring rules; Balance of Power nuclear-war screen; Frostpunk 'But was it worth it?'.

findings.title: Checkpoint timing invites a Q4-1954 aid dump; the paper must print standing from a trailing window so gaming is visible and dull
findings.detail: Twilight Struggle players time coups to scoring cards; with fixed public dates at 1955/1960/1965 every bloc will withdraw aid from Europe and pour it into the narrowest region in the months before a reckoning, and the Reckoning page will reward that spike. The legible fix is presentation-side and cheap: the frozen standing counts a battleground only if it has been in the band for at least 6 of the last 12 months (the influence system already tracks last_band_change and 12-month hysteresis), and the MOVERS list prints when a country crossed ('IRAQ: EAST SINCE NOV 1954 -- NOT YET ON THE RECORD'). A country that flipped in December reads as pending, which the player sees and understands, instead of a hidden rule. This also makes the trend arrows honest: standing is a 12-month fact, not a snapshot.
findings.evidence: docs/design/systems/influence.md 'Formulas' (BAND_ENTER/BAND_LEAVE, REVERSAL_MONTHS = 12, last_band_change); Twilight Struggle scoring-card timing meta (GMT forums / BoardGameGeek strategy threads, 2006-2015).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE STANDING LINE — monthly verdict sentence in the paper's WORLD IN NUMBERS rail, mirrored as a one-word HUD chip
mechanics_recommendations.why: Tells the player how they are doing without a number, changes at most once a month, and always carries a cause and a verb pointer (no panel without a verb). Reuses the momentum-assessment template from war_ui.rs and the existing monthly standings, RegionSnapshots, legitimacy and tension resources.
mechanics_recommendations.how: At month rollover compute four signed integer columns for the player: ALIGNMENT (battleground regions held/denied vs par), OUTPUT (national industry index vs par; planner reads REPORTED, market reads lagged), PRESTIGE (legitimacy plus firsts: bomb, H-bomb, deliverable deterrent), CATASTROPHE (months above Crisis band, wars begun, nuclear use, satellites crushed — always non-positive). Verdict word from the sign of the sum vs par with a dead band: LEADING / EVEN / TRAILING; cause = column with the largest contribution in the verdict's direction, rendered as a noun phrase with the region or figure ('ASIA RUNS AGAINST US', 'THE PLAN IS BEHIND', 'THE PEACE IS COSTING US'); pointer = panel key. Paper line: 'OUR STANDING: TRAILING -- ASIA RUNS AGAINST US [P] -- NEXT RECKONING JAN 1955'. Bloc leaders get a second line 'HEAD TO HEAD: PROBABLY LEADING MOSCOW (EST.)' with the Kent qualifier when the rival estimate width exceeds the margin. HUD chip shows the word only, tooltip repeats the sentence, click opens the paper at the rail. Word set and dead band are tuning constants; if the estimate is wider than the margin the word is 'EVEN', never a coin flip.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE RECKONING — a special edition of the paper at 1955-01-01, 1960-01-01, 1965-01-01 (and 1970-01-01 as the final)
mechanics_recommendations.why: The era checkpoint is the one moment a table is allowed; it is the Twilight Struggle scoring card as a newspaper page and it must be readable in under a minute, for any of 86 nations, in the player's own bloc voice.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Layout, top to bottom: (1) computed banner headline from a 6-template set ('WEST LEADS AT THE HALF-DECADE; ASIA THE PRIZE' / 'MOSCOW CLAIMS THE DECADE; WASHINGTON DISPUTES IT'). (2) WHERE WE STAND: four rows (ALIGNMENT, OUTPUT, PRESTIGE, CATASTROPHE) × three columns: OURS (exact word + figure), THEIRS (bracket at 2 sig figs, AS-OF stamp, '?' below LIMITED coverage), VERDICT (STRONG / HOLDING / WEAK plus an arrow only if two consecutive reckonings agree). (3) THE MAP BY REGION: the six regions with the existing standing verdict words and counts, the narrowest margin marked 'THE PRIZE'. (4) MOVERS: top three gains and top three losses since the last reckoning, each 'COUNTRY: BAND SINCE DATE -- CAUSE' from the existing wire-cause machinery; entries in band fewer than 6 of 12 months print 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD'. (5) AS THEY SEE IT: two lines rendered from the rival's REPORTED figures and standings in their masthead voice ('PRAVDA: THE SOCIALIST CAMP LEADS IN ASIA AND AFRICA; PLAN FULFILLED 108%'), so claim vs estimate is visible. (6) THE VERDICT: one sentence vs par and, for bloc leaders, head to head; then 'WHAT DECIDED IT: ...' one line; then 'NEXT RECKONING: JAN 1960 -- WATCH: MIDDLE EAST (1 STATE FROM DOMINATION)'. Frozen text stored with the checkpoint so the page is re-readable from the archive and a test can string-compare it across seeds. Caps: 4 rows, 6 regions, 6 movers, 2 claim lines, 3 verdict lines — fits without scrolling.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE EPILOGUE — campaign verdict at 1970-01-01 and on general exchange, in two vocabularies
mechanics_recommendations.why: Produces the campaign verdict the vision promises, keeps the big war un-winnable in the only place it matters (the sentence the player screenshots), and satisfies the Suzerain/Frostpunk lesson that an ending is legible only when each line names its cause.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Normal ending (1970): screen 1 is one verdict sentence from a fixed vocabulary vs par — BEAT THE CENTURY / HELD THE LINE / LOST THE DECADE — with the head-to-head for bloc leaders ('THE WEST BEAT THE CENTURY; THE EAST HELD THE LINE'), then THE THREE THINGS THAT DECIDED IT: the three (column, checkpoint-or-event) contributions with the largest absolute value, ties broken by date then tag, each templated with a date and a deep fact ('1956: SUEZ COST YOU THE ARAB WORLD (3 BATTLEGROUNDS EAST BY 1960)', 'YOU NEVER BUILT THE BOMB: PRESTIGE WEAK AT EVERY RECKONING'). Screen 2 is the four Reckonings side by side as words. Catastrophe ending: keep the existing funeral screen verbatim (cities, exact dead, initiator, how long the peace held, 'WE DO NOT REWARD FAILURE'); append one page, no table: 'THE RECORD ENDS HERE.' plus the standing as of the last paper ('YOU WERE LEADING. IT DID NOT MATTER.') and the three things that led to the exchange (crisis rungs, first use, alert dial) with dates. Vocabulary for it is RUIN only; the word LEADING may appear only in the past tense. A tactical or demonstration use that does not end the game writes a permanent CATASTROPHE line that every later Reckoning and the epilogue repeat ('THE TABOO WAS BROKEN AT ... , 1953').

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE HISTORICAL PAR — a shipped data table that makes one scoring rule serve all 86 nations
mechanics_recommendations.why: Removes the need for a second scoring system for middle and minor powers, gives day-one targets, and is deterministic and free at runtime because the comparison is a lookup.
mechanics_recommendations.how: During scenario build, run the hands-off harness and record each nation's four column values at 1955/1960/1965/1970 into assets/data/scenario/1950/par.ron (generated, never hand-edited, validated at load). At runtime the verdict compares the player's columns to par with a dead band per column; bloc leaders additionally compare to the rival's estimate. The founding edition prints THE RECORD SAYS for the player's nation in words ('BY 1955 THE RECORD HAS EUROPE HOLDING AND CHINA LOST; BEAT IT.'), so the first hour already has a legible target. Par for a nation born after 1950 starts at its birth checkpoint; a nation that ceases to exist gets 'THE RECORD ENDS' and the last standing as verdict.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE ONE-MINUTE ERA SUMMARY — a fixed 80-word card, reused by the Reckoning, the archive, and the epilogue
mechanics_recommendations.why: The brief asks for an era readable in under a minute; a card with a hard word budget is the only way to guarantee it and to keep the page from growing into a ledger.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Five lines, mono 10pt, right rail: line 1 verdict sentence; lines 2-5 one per column, 'ALIGNMENT: HOLDING -- EUROPE FIRM, ASIA WEAK'; footer line 'DECIDED BY: ...' and 'WATCH: ...'. Every line ends in the panel key that owns it. The same card is what the HUD chip's click opens mid-era (with 'AS OF' the last paper), what the checkpoint page leads with, and what the epilogue stacks four of. Word count is asserted in a test.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: PUBLISH THE RULE ONCE, IN WORDS — 'HOW THE CENTURY IS SCORED' box in the founding edition
mechanics_recommendations.why: A deterministic public formula will be reverse-engineered anyway (Twilight Struggle, EU4 age objectives); stating it in period prose stops players hunting for hidden weights and tells minors what counts for them.
mechanics_recommendations.how: A fixed text box in the January 1950 founding edition and the manual: the four columns, the checkpoint dates, that non-aligned counts against both blocs, that standing is a twelve-month fact, that catastrophes are never forgiven, and that a general exchange ends the record. No numbers, no percentages; weights live in a tuning module and the design doc.

pitfalls: A HUD score number or progress bar: any live figure converts the four pillars into one meter and reintroduces the watching-a-simulation feeling the research repeatedly names; show one word that can change only at month rollover.

Verdict flicker: if the word is recomputed from raw monthly values without a dead band and a two-month trend rule, EVEN/TRAILING oscillates on noise and the player learns to ignore it (Vic3 prestige jitter).

Estimate-driven flips: letting the rival's fuzzed column decide LEADING vs TRAILING makes the verdict jitter with the intel sample; qualify with Kent words or fall back to EVEN when the bracket exceeds the margin.
An 86-row ranking or a score-over-time chart: minors read as perpetual losers and superpowers read a causeless line; print only you, the rival estimate, and the movers.
Uninformative causes: 'ALIGNMENT' as the cause is a column name, not a reason; the template must name the region, figure or event and the panel that acts on it, otherwise the acceptance test fails.

A catastrophe screen that ranks: any table, medal or 'winner' under the mushroom cloud makes the big war winnable in the player's mind regardless of the formula; the exchange page has no numbers except the dead.

Checkpoint gaming reads as a hidden rule: if December flips count in full, players dump aid before reckonings; if they are silently discounted, it reads as a bug. Print 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD' on the mover line.

Percentages and permille leaking into the Reckoning via econ figures ('PLAN FULFILLED 103%' is diegetic and allowed only as the rival's claim line or the planner's own reported figure; verdict columns are words).
Founding edition without a target: if the first paper shows a standing word with no par line, the player has no idea what LEADING would even mean until 1955; the record line must be there on day one.
Epilogue that reveals the formula by listing every term: three things, dated, is the whole point; a twelve-line breakdown becomes the EU4 ledger at the funeral.
analysts.first_hour_test: Jan 1950 founding edition (opened with N on the paused start screen): the WORLD IN NUMBERS rail carries 'OUR STANDING: EVEN -- THE RECORD BEGINS' plus THE RECORD SAYS for the player's nation in one sentence (e.g. USA: 'BY 1955 THE RECORD HAS EUROPE HOLDING, CHINA LOST AND KOREA DIVIDED; BEAT IT.'; Egypt: 'BY 1955 THE RECORD HAS THE CANAL STILL BRITISH AND THE MONARCHY GONE.'), and the HOW THE CENTURY IS SCORED box; the HUD shows one chip reading EVEN and nothing numeric about score anywhere. Feb through Jun 1950 monthly editions: the standing line appears every month with a cause and a panel key; across the five months the word changes at most once, every change has a wire line naming the cause, and the line ends with 'NEXT RECKONING: JAN 1955 (5X MONTHS)'. By July 1950 the Korean outbreak writes the first CATASTROPHE entry ('WAR IN ASIA -- ON THE RECORD AGAINST BOTH BLOCS') visible in the rail. Acceptance, first hour: a tester playing USA, SOV, EGY and LUX each, having opened only the paper, can say in one sentence which column is dragging their standing and which key to press to act on it; for LUX (0 slots) the pointer is still a real verb ('[E] ECONOMY' or 'TREATY'). At the first checkpoint (1955-01-01, reached in a hands-off harness run): the Reckoning special edition prints the four-row table with OURS exact, THEIRS as a bracket with an AS-OF stamp (or '?' with 'MOSCOW DOES NOT PUBLISH'), six regional verdict words with one marked THE PRIZE, up to six movers with dates and causes and at least one 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD' where a December flip exists, two AS THEY SEE IT lines rendered from the rival's reported figures, and a verdict sentence vs par that matches the historian anchors (hands-off USA reads HELD THE LINE / EVEN, never LEADING); the page fits without scrolling, the era summary is under 80 words, and a same-seed second run produces byte-identical page text.

findings.title: One formula fits all 86 nations only if the formula is 'standing in a column over a reach set', with the column and the reach set as data — not a per-nation ruleset
findings.detail: The vision's four terms (bloc alignment, economic output, prestige, avoided catastrophes) already collapse into four lines the sim can compute for ANY country from existing state: STANDING = sum over the nation's REACH regions of weight x (battlegrounds in MY column) minus (battlegrounds in the RIVAL column), where 'my column' is West, East or DENIED depending on the nation's pole (a non-aligned Egypt or India scores the denied column — which is exactly what Nehru and Nasser were playing for); PROSPERITY = standard of living against the nation's own 1950 figure and against the visible rival-bloc standard (economy.md already specifies relative SoL, 'the kitchen debate as a mechanic'); SECURITY = sovereign, unoccupied, un-couped, stability band, no lock imposed against the nation's will; PEACE = a world line (taboo intact, no exchange, war dead this era as a share of world population, crises closed below Firebreak A) with a personal attribution sub-line (your casualties per capita, rungs you climbed). The USA and USSR have reach = all six regions and column = their pole; the UK has reach EUROPE+MIDDLE_EAST+AFRICA; India reach ASIA, column DENIED; Yugoslavia reach EUROPE, column DENIED; Guatemala reach CENTRAL_AMERICA, column DENIED under Arbenz (or West after a flip). What differs per nation is not the arithmetic but the EXPECTATION row: a sourced target per checkpoint per line, so the same four lines print AHEAD / ON COURSE / BEHIND / FAILING. This is the Football Manager board-expectations model: every club is judged on the one league table, but Luton's board asks 'avoid relegation' and Manchester United's asks 'win the title'. Victoria 2's Great Power rank (prestige + industrial score + military score, one table for 200+ nations, with Great/Secondary/other tiers) is the grand-strategy precedent that a single world score with a per-nation share works for minors; what Vic2 lacked was the expectation row, so Belgium at rank 14 never knew whether that was good.
findings.evidence: Existing state: `Influence.standings` / `checkpoints` with per-region west/east/denied and Verdict::{None,Presence,Domination,Control} (crates/ugs-sim/src/influence.rs lines 103, 223-226, 2174-2210; battleground set with weights 1-3 and per-region thresholds in assets/data/scenario/1950/influence.ron lines 256-346); `LivingStandards.by_country` (SoL 5-80, demography.rs line 88-92); `Settlements.legitimacy` -100..100 (settlement.rs line 256); `Military.casualties` (military.rs line 296); `Programs.taboo_broken` (nuclear.rs line 226); `Military.stability` overrides (world-timeline.md). Relative SoL: docs/design/systems/economy.md 'Cross-bloc scoreboard'. Football Manager (Sports Interactive, every edition since FM2005): board expectations per club on one league table. Victoria 2 (Paradox, 2010) Great Power ranking formula. Old World (Mohawk Games, 2021): 'Ambitions' drawn from the player's situation, victory by completing ten of them — per-situation goals without per-nation rules.

findings.title: 'Beat history' beats 'beat the hands-off AI' as the baseline, provided the expectation rows are OUTCOMES (rank, SoL delta, sovereignty, column counts) rather than events — and every archetype has a sourced, dated self-declared 1970 target to anchor it
findings.detail: The Soviet Union literally published its scorecard: Khrushchev's 22 May 1957 'catch up and overtake America' in per-capita meat, milk and butter, and the Third Party Programme (22nd Congress, October 1961) promising to surpass US per-capita industrial output by 1970 and lay 'the material and technical basis of communism' by 1980. That is the USSR's PROSPERITY expectation row for 1970 in its own words, and the planned player reads it against REPORTED figures — the ledger that lies to its own planner is the epistemic texture the house rules demand. The US target is NSC-68 (14 April 1950): 'frustrate the Kremlin design' and build 'situations of strength' without wrecking the economy (Eisenhower's 'Great Equation' of security and solvency, 1953) — so the American 1955 row is HOLD Europe, DENY Asia, keep PROSPERITY LEADING; holding the lead is enough only if PEACE holds and legitimacy does not bleed, which is why the 1950-55 US player's real test is Korea's aim ladder (crossing the 38th costs legitimacy -10 and tension +25 in the existing table). The UK row is managed decline with a floor: West Germany overtook British GDP around 1959-60 and Japan in 1968; Acheson's West Point line (5 December 1962) 'lost an empire and not yet found a role' is the FAILING sentence; the UK beats history by holding rank three in 1970 and East of Suez past January 1968. India's row is Panchsheel (April 1954) and Bandung (April 1955): DENIED count in ASIA rising, SECURITY not broken by the 1962 border war. Yugoslavia: not crushed, not re-locked, Belgrade Conference (September 1961) founding NAM. Egypt: the auction — Czech arms deal (27 September 1955), Aswan (19 July 1956) — measured as both chequebooks naming EGY while EGY stays in the denied column. Guatemala: still sovereign under Arbenz after June 1954 with Decree 900 (June 1952) intact; beating history there is the whole campaign. The hands-off baseline ('the world without you') is attractive because the sim already runs 20 hands-off years in ~15 s deterministically, but it makes the player's own nation an AI-run counterfactual, costs a background run per seed, and the comparison reads as a mirror-match, not a story. Keep it as a v2 flourish at the 1970 retrospective ('THE WORLD WITHOUT YOU'), not the score.
findings.evidence: Khrushchev speech 22 May 1957 (Leningrad, agricultural workers); CPSU Third Programme adopted 31 October 1961; NSC-68 dated 14 April 1950; Acheson, West Point, 5 December 1962; UK 'East of Suez' withdrawal announced 16 January 1968; Sino-Indian War 20 Oct - 21 Nov 1962; Belgrade Conference 1-6 September 1961; Kennedy, The Rise and Fall of the Great Powers (1987) on relative-decline metrics; Westad, The Global Cold War (2005) on the Third World as the scoring ground. Repo: `the_world_turns_to_1970` (~15 s, world-timeline.md) and `hands_off_anchors_land_near_history` (influence.rs line 2968) prove a hands-off baseline is computable but not free. War-aim price table AIM_TENSION [0,10,25,60] / AIM_LEGITIMACY [0,0,-10,-25] in war-termination.md.

findings.title: The pyrrhic rule: never score the exchange; cap the verdict for the one who broke the taboo; let the crisis system, not the score, do the deterring
findings.detail: Three precedents mark the boundaries. Balance of Power (Chris Crawford, 1985) ends nuclear war with 'We do not reward failure' and no screen — the repo already adopts Crawford's rule in endgame.rs. DEFCON (Introversion, 2006) went the other way and scored the exchange (Default mode +2 per million enemy dead, -1 per million own dead; Genocide and Survivor modes) and became a game ABOUT megadeath optimisation — the exact exploit the brief forbids. Twilight Struggle (GMT, 2005) makes the player who drops DEFCON to 1 lose outright, which is the right instinct but too binary for a twenty-year real-time campaign where the vision says the loss is shared. Recommended shape: (a) General exchange: no verdict class for anyone. The funeral screen already prints cities, exact dead and attribution; add Herman Kahn's own format — the 'Tragic but Distinguishable Postwar States' table (On Thermonuclear War, 1960: 2 million dead vs 160 million, 'Will the survivors envy the dead?') printed for both homelands, and one line: 'BY THE LEDGER, [NATION] WON. THE LEDGER IS ALL THAT SURVIVED.' The campaign record stores it as class EXCHANGE, unrankable, below every other outcome including RUIN. Even a ONE-SIDED 1950-55 dyad exchange (US v USSR before Soviet two-way reach ~1956) gets this: the vision's 'winning one is pyrrhic' is served by an honest table, not by a bonus. (b) Limited use (the MacArthur chain, `taboo_broken`): the campaign continues, and the score neither subtracts nor zeroes — it applies a VERDICT CEILING: the breaker's best attainable campaign class becomes SURVIVED, printed as a permanent masthead line ('VERDICT CEILING: SURVIVOR — THE TABOO, BROKEN AT [PLACE], [DATE]'). A ceiling rather than a subtraction matters for two reasons: a subtraction makes limited use a computable trade against the province it wins (an exploit), while a zero makes the remaining fifteen years pointless (a quit); a ceiling keeps every other line worth playing for rank-within-class. (c) The 'nothing to lose' trailer who nukes freely is not a scoring problem: the existing mechanics already answer it — a patron ultimatum crisis at rung 6, everyone's use thresholds dropping, neutral alignment collapsing, the AI launching at resolve 95+. The score's job is only to refuse the reward. Name it what Plutarch named it: Pyrrhus after Asculum, 'one more such victory and we are utterly undone' — the verdict word PYRRHIC is a fact about the ledger, not an editorial.
findings.evidence: crates/ugs-app/src/endgame.rs lines 1-5 (Crawford's rule quoted in the module doc); crisis.rs lines 341-368 (GameOver: dead = 60% of every city >= 300k in both homelands, tension to 1000); nuclear.rs line 225-226 (Tannenwald taboo flag), line 505-506 (AI escalation gates read taboo_broken and resolve >= 85/95). findings.title: Anti-snowball is already half-built into the world and needs no rubber band: the pie grows (decolonization), the record is fogged (the missile gap), the end is weighted (history remembers how it ended), and prestige shocks are earnable
findings.detail: Civilization's runaway leader (Sid Meier, GDC 2010 'Everything You Know Is Wrong': players who feel they are losing at turn 100 quit) and Paradox's late-game slump (EU4 and HoI4 forums are full of 'the game is decided by 1600 / 1942'; HoI4 has no victory condition at all and simply runs to its end date) are the two failure cases. Fixes that worked elsewhere: Civ VI Rise and Fall (February 2018) re-baselined Era Score thresholds every era so a leader must keep earning and a Dark Age can flip to a Heroic Age; EU4 1.25 'Rule Britannia' (March 2018) gave every age its own seven objectives so old leads stop compounding; Twilight Struggle's Space Race track is an explicit catch-up valve (dump a bad card, earn VP) that reads as history. UGS has four historical equivalents, three of which already exist: (1) The battleground set is effectively re-issued by decolonization — the Year of Africa (1960, seventeen new states) opens 24-month contested windows with doubled rates; a 1955 leader in Europe finds Africa's column empty in 1960. Make this legible: the paper's COLONIAL QUESTION table should say how many battlegrounds are 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD' so the trailer sees the open pie. (2) The rival's lines print as ESTIMATES with intel-width brackets — the leader can never be sure they lead. This is the missile gap (Gaither Report, November 1957; Kennedy's 1960 campaign; debunked by Gilpatric on 21 October 1961): the fogged score is a unique anti-coasting device no other game has, and it falls straight out of the house rule that foreign numbers are estimates. (3) Weight the checkpoints toward the end — 1955:1, 1960:2, 1965:3, 1970:4 — and print a TRAJECTORY word (RISING / HOLDING / DECLINING) beside every checkpoint class, so a 1960 trailer who is rising has a 1970 to play for and a 1960 leader who is declining is told so. (4) Prestige shocks as Great Projects with era deadlines: first satellite, first orbit, first thermonuclear test, the moon — each a sourced 'FIRST' on the record (Sputnik 4 October 1957 cost the US far more standing than any battleground flip) bought with the crash-program posture at consumer-goods cost. The trailing superpower can buy a shock; the leader must answer it (the existing `sputnik-crash-program` chain). This is the vision's 'prestige' term made mechanical without a second world-opinion currency: legitimacy stays the currency; FIRSTS are events on the record.
findings.evidence: Sid Meier, GDC 2010 keynote; Civilization VI: Rise and Fall (Firaxis, 8 Feb 2018) era score / Dark-Heroic ages; EU4 patch 1.25 (Paradox, 20 Mar 2018) Ages and age objectives; Twilight Struggle Space Race track; Paradox forum threads 'HoI4 has no win condition' (recurring since 2016 release); Gaither Report 7 Nov 1957; Gilpatric speech 21 Oct 1961. Repo: contested windows and doubled rates (influence.md 'Decolonization'); `sputnik` / `sputnik-crash-program` / Apollo chain in assets/data/scenario/1950/events/04-superpower-systemic-arc-.ron lines 71-193; estimate helpers (`intel_width`, 2-sig-fig fuzz) shared by paper and dossiers (newspaper.md Epistemics).

findings.title: The AI rival should be score-AWARE (it reads the same public standings and the checkpoint calendar) but never score-CHASING (it never reads the player's ledger or expectation rows)
findings.detail: Players enjoy rivals with visible goals — Civ VI's leader agendas (2016) are the most-cited thing the AI does right, and Old World's AI pursues the same Ambitions the player does — but they hate an AI that reads their hidden score (Civ V's AI hunting the human when a victory nears reads as cheating). The influence allocator today scores candidates by weight x population x (1000 - |pos|) x contested, with no rival-activity multiplier, and drops a program at +600. Two deterministic additions make it play the era without touching player state: (a) a MARGINAL-REGION weight — multiply candidate score by 2 when the region's verdict for the sponsor would step up (PRESENCE to DOMINATION, or a rival CONTROL would be broken) by that one flip, read from `standings` which is public and printed monthly, the same logic as a Twilight Struggle player holding a scoring card; (b) a PRE-RECKONING SURGE — in the twelve months before a checkpoint freeze the allocator fills every slot and the AI prefers AID over PRESENCE if the pool covers it; historically this is election-year behaviour and the 1959-60 Soviet economic offensive. Both are printed in the rival's chequebook so the player sees the rival playing the calendar. What the AI must NOT do: read the player's expectation rows, target the player's reach set specifically, or vary by difficulty via score bonuses (Civ's difficulty-scaled production bonuses are the rubber band the brief forbids). Since the standings are already fogged for the player but exact for the sim, the AI reading exact standings is a small, honest asymmetry — the paper should say so ('MOSCOW KEEPS ITS OWN COUNT').
findings.evidence: AI allocator score and rules in influence.md 'AI allocator' and 'AI note' (no rival multiplier, AI_DONE = 600 at influence.rs line 98, AI_POOL_RESERVE 900); post-slice item 2 'AI election pushes and coups through the same allocator'. Civilization VI leader agendas (Firaxis, Oct 2016); Old World AI ambitions (Mohawk, 2021); Twilight Struggle scoring-card play; the 'Soviet economic offensive' event in events/09-influence-1950-1970.ron.

findings.title: Checkpoint gaming is real (Twilight Struggle proves it is fun in a card game and a trap here) — score the year on the record, not the tick of the freeze
findings.detail: In Twilight Struggle the scoring-card timing game is the whole skill, because the card is hidden. UGS checkpoint dates are public (first tick of 1955/1960/1965), so a freeze read at one tick invites a December aid surge and a coup timed to resolve on 30 December. The influence system already has partial protection (band entry needs |pos| >= 300 evaluated at a month rollover; reversal within 12 months runs at half rate; a coup takes 90 days), but PROSPERITY and SECURITY have none. Recommendation: every ledger line freezes as the trailing twelve-month mean of its monthly value ('THE YEAR ON THE RECORD'), which is what the reckoning edition should say it is. It costs twelve integers per line per nation, it is deterministic, and it converts a burst into a trend — a player who wants the 1960 record must hold Iraq through 1959, not buy it in December. The same trailing window is what makes the TRAJECTORY word computable for free (compare this checkpoint's mean to the last).
findings.evidence: BAND_ENTER 300 / BAND_LEAVE 150 / REVERSAL_MONTHS 12 / COUP_PREP_DAYS 90 in influence.md 'Formulas'; CHECKPOINT_YEARS [1955,1960,1965] at influence.rs line 104 and the freeze at lines 1993-2003 (a one-tick copy today). Twilight Struggle (GMT 2005) scoring-card mechanics; Gupta and Matthews designer notes in the rulebook.

findings.title: Show the verdict as a period document, not a scoreboard, and never editorialise it: Frostpunk's 'But was it worth it?' is the cautionary tale, Suzerain's epilogues the model, the paper the surface
findings.detail: Frostpunk (11 bit studios, April 2018) ends a survived campaign with 'The city survived. But was it worth it?' if the player went far down the Order or Faith book — and the line drew a sustained backlash (Steam forums and r/Frostpunk threads from launch week on) because it judged players who had no other way to survive; Frostpunk 2 (2024) dropped the line for faction-relationship endings. Suzerain (Torpor Games, December 2020) has no score at all: the epilogue is a set of dated slides per faction and person, and players discuss endings by their outcome states, not numbers. UGS already has the right surface: the paper prints a RECKONING at each freeze and the war-legibility rules forbid raw percentages. So the 1970 verdict is a twenty-page retrospective edition — 'THE DECADE IN REVIEW' — with the four lines as headed columns, each carrying its expectation sentence, its band word, its trajectory, the three named causes that moved it most (from the wire ring), and the rival's lines as estimates. The campaign class (TRIUMPH / VICTORY / HELD / SURVIVED / DECLINE / RUIN, with PYRRHIC and EXCHANGE as ceiling classes) is one word in the masthead, sourced from the ledger, never from a moral. A separate DIVERGENCES column lists the first five points where the world left history (OptionChosen chains, Independence dates missed, wars that did not happen), which is both the replay hook and the honest answer to 'was it worth it': the player reads what changed and decides. During the campaign the same four lines sit in THE WORLD IN NUMBERS rail every month with an AS-OF stamp, and each line is a deep link to the panel that moves it (the 'no panel without a verb' rule): STANDING to the politics panel, PROSPERITY to the economy panel, PEACE to the crisis/atomic dossier, SECURITY to the domestic events log.
findings.evidence: Frostpunk ending text and reception (11 bit, 2018; Steam Community threads April-May 2018); Frostpunk 2 (11 bit, Sept 2024) ending structure; Suzerain epilogue design (Torpor, 2020). Repo: RECKONING line at crates/ugs-app/src/paper_ui.rs line 596; section registry in newspaper.md; wire ring of 60 with named causes (influence.md State); OptionChosen chain trigger (world-timeline.md); house rules in docs/research/economic-agency.md principles 1, 2, 7 and war-legibility.

findings.title: The 'do-nothing' turtle is a real exploit of any avoided-catastrophe score, and the fix is Twilight Struggle's military-ops requirement translated into expectation rows that demand movement from the superpowers
findings.detail: If PEACE and SECURITY are lines and the player can score by never opening a crisis, the dominant USA strategy is to sit on 1950 (already ahead) and let tension decay to the floor — Paradox's 'tall' turtle and EU4's no-war ironman runs are the pattern. Twilight Struggle solved it with the Military Operations track: a player who does not conduct enough ops each turn loses VP, so restraint costs something. UGS should not import a penalty term; it should import the expectation. The superpower rows demand movement: the USA's 1955 row is DENY ASIA (a Korea armistice that holds AND Japan in band AND Indochina not lost), its 1960 row is PRESENCE in AFRICA (the Year of Africa windows) — you cannot meet them by sitting still; the USSR's rows demand PROSPERITY RISING by 1960 and Asia PRESENCE by 1955 (the Sino-Soviet treaty lock), which cannot be met without spending the pool. Middle powers and minors, by contrast, are ALLOWED to score by surviving, because for Guatemala or Yugoslavia surviving IS beating history. This asymmetry lives in the data rows, not in the formula, which is the whole point of the expectation table.
findings.evidence: Twilight Struggle rule 8.2 Military Operations track (GMT 2005, 2nd printing errata); Paradox forum discussions of 'tall' play in EU4 and the 'no-war' meta; NSC-68's explicit rejection of containment-by-inaction. Repo: the Sino-Soviet treaty lock on Peking until the split (influence.md Implementation status); Korea aim ladder and armistice-as-FrozenConflict (war-termination.md Layer 4).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE LEDGER: four banded lines, one formula, per-nation expectation rows in data (assets/data/scenario/1950/expectations.ron)
mechanics_recommendations.why: Serves USSR, USA, middle and minor powers with one scoring system: the arithmetic is shared (STANDING over a reach set in a column; PROSPERITY vs own 1950 and vs the visible rival standard; SECURITY; PEACE with personal attribution) and only the expectation targets, reach regions and column differ per nation. Every input already exists as integer BTreeMap state; monthly work hangs off `new_month`; no new RNG. Replaces the vision's 'prestige' with legitimacy plus a FIRSTS register so there is still exactly one world-opinion currency.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Monthly, in TickSet::Politics after `update_influence`, compute per playable nation: STANDING = sum over reach regions of weight x (battlegrounds in my column) - (in rival column), with my column = West / East / DENIED per the nation's pole; PROSPERITY = SoL now minus SoL 1950 (planner reads REPORTED), plus the sign of SoL vs the rival bloc's visible standard; SECURITY = sovereign AND unoccupied AND no successful coup AND stability band, minus imposed locks; PEACE = world (taboo intact, no exchange, era war dead as permille of world population, crises closed below R5) plus attribution (own casualties per capita, rungs climbed by you). Each line is banded against the nation's expectation row for the NEXT checkpoint into AHEAD / ON COURSE / BEHIND / FAILING and printed as a verdict sentence with its top three named causes from the wire ring. Expectation rows are sourced per playable nation for 1955/1960/1965/1970 (Khrushchev 1957/1961 for SOV, NSC-68 for USA, Acheson/East-of-Suez for UK, Panchsheel/Bandung for IND, Belgrade for YUG, the auction for EGY, 'still sovereign' for GTM); a nation with no row falls back to the archetype row (superpower / middle / minor) by 1950 industry rank. Every line in the paper's WORLD IN NUMBERS rail is a deep link to the panel whose verbs move it.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE YEAR ON THE RECORD: trailing-twelve-month checkpoints, end-weighted campaign class, and a TRAJECTORY word
mechanics_recommendations.why: Kills December-surge checkpoint gaming (public freeze dates make it inevitable otherwise), gives a 1960 trailer a reason to stay (RISING is a verdict) and a 1960 leader a reason not to coast (DECLINING is too), and makes 1970 the checkpoint that matters most, which is how history remembers eras.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Each ledger line keeps a ring of its last twelve monthly values; the freeze at 1955/1960/1965/1970 stores the mean, not the tick value, and the reckoning edition says so. Campaign class at 1970 (or at catastrophe) = weighted sum of checkpoint bands with weights 1/2/3/4 for 1955/1960/1965/1970, mapped to TRIUMPH / VICTORY / HELD / SURVIVED / DECLINE / RUIN; the TRAJECTORY word compares this checkpoint's mean to the last and prints beside every class. Weights and class cut-offs live in a `ledger::tuning` module.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: VERDICT CEILINGS instead of penalties for the catastrophes: taboo broken by you caps at SURVIVED; general exchange is class EXCHANGE, unrankable, for everyone; the Kahn table replaces any score on the funeral screen
mechanics_recommendations.why: A subtraction makes limited nuclear use a computable trade against the province it wins (exploit); a zero makes the rest of the campaign pointless (quit); a ceiling keeps every line worth playing for rank-within-class while guaranteeing the big war is never win-able on the record. Deterrence stays where it belongs — the patron ultimatum crisis, the AI's dropped thresholds, collapsing neutral alignment — and the score only refuses the reward (Crawford's rule, already adopted in endgame.rs).
mechanics_recommendations.how: On `taboo_broken` with the player as user: set `ceiling = Survived` on the player's ledger, print a permanent masthead line 'VERDICT CEILING: SURVIVOR — THE TABOO BROKEN AT [PROVINCE], [DATE]'; the class computation clamps to the ceiling. On `GameOver`: no class for any nation; the funeral screen adds Kahn's 'tragic but distinguishable postwar states' table for both homelands (dead, cities, share of 1950 population) and the single line 'BY THE LEDGER, [INITIATOR/AGAINST] WON. THE LEDGER IS ALL THAT SURVIVED.'; the hall of records stores it as EXCHANGE below RUIN. Imposed unrecognised annexation and CRUSH do not cap — they already pay in legitimacy and tension, which the STANDING and PEACE lines read.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE FOGGED SCORE: the rival's ledger lines print as intelligence estimates with brackets; own lines exact (planners: REPORTED)
mechanics_recommendations.why: The unique anti-coasting device: a leader who cannot verify the lead keeps playing (the missile gap of 1957-61 was exactly this). It costs nothing new — the paper's estimate helpers and the 2-significant-figure fuzz already exist — and it is the pillar-3 signature applied to the score itself. Planners reading REPORTED prosperity is the pillar-4 signature applied to the score.
mechanics_recommendations.how: In the monthly rail and the reckoning edition, render the rival superpower's four lines through the existing `intel_width`/estimate helpers keyed on political and economic penetration: 'EAST STANDING: PROBABLY BEHIND (EST. 9-13 STATES)'; own planned PROSPERITY prints the reported SoL with the existing padding and the AUDIT verb when it lands. The AI reads exact standings (sim truth) and the paper says so once: 'MOSCOW KEEPS ITS OWN COUNT'.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: SCORE-AWARE RIVAL: marginal-region weight and pre-reckoning surge in the existing allocator; never reads player ledgers or difficulty bonuses
mechanics_recommendations.why: Players like rivals with visible goals (Civ VI agendas, Old World ambitions) and hate rivals that read hidden scores or get rubber-band bonuses; the allocator already has a candidate score and a public standings table to read.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Multiply candidate score by 2 when flipping that battleground would step the sponsor's regional verdict up or break a rival CONTROL, read from `standings`; in the twelve months before a freeze fill every slot and prefer AID over PRESENCE when the pool covers tier 1. Both behaviours surface in the printed chequebook so the player can see the calendar being played. No read of the player's expectation rows or reach set; no score-scaled bonuses at any difficulty.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: FIRSTS on the record and the growing pie made legible
mechanics_recommendations.why: Historical catch-up dynamics rather than rubber bands: Sputnik (4 October 1957) moved standing more than any battleground and was bought with a crash program at consumer cost; the Year of Africa (1960) re-issued the battleground set. Both exist in the timeline; the ledger should count them.
mechanics_recommendations.how: A `firsts` register (first satellite, first orbit, first thermonuclear test, first man on the moon — each a sourced Great Project with an era deadline gated by the nuclear/industrial substrate, attributable to whoever finishes first) adds a fixed legitimacy grant and a named line in STANDING's causes; the COLONIAL QUESTION table gains a 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD: N BATTLEGROUNDS' line counting unborn sourced battlegrounds so a trailer sees the open pie at 1955.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: THE DECADE IN REVIEW: the 1970 (or catastrophe) verdict as a retrospective newspaper edition with a DIVERGENCES column and a per-nation hall of records
mechanics_recommendations.why: Suzerain's epilogues and the existing paper are the right surface; Frostpunk's editorial line is the wrong one. A divergence chronicle is the replay hook — a second campaign is different in score terms because the expectation rows differ by nation, the rival plays the calendar differently per seed, and the record shows where your world left history.
mechanics_recommendations.how: At 1970-01-01 (or on `GameOver`/`taboo_broken` ceiling) render a special edition: masthead class word, four headed columns (expectation sentence, band, trajectory, top three causes), rival lines as estimates, the Kahn table if applicable, and DIVERGENCES (first five OptionChosen branches or missed/early Independence dates versus the sourced calendar). Persist a `records.ron` per nation with class, ceiling, checkpoints and seed; the nation-select screen shows the best class per nation so the second campaign has a bar to beat.

pitfalls: Scoring the exchange at all (DEFCON's +2 per million killed) — any positive term for a survived exchange turns the campaign into a first-strike optimisation problem; the only safe output is a table of the dead and an unrankable class.

Moralising the verdict (Frostpunk's 'But was it worth it?') — print the ledger, the class word and the divergences; let the player judge. PYRRHIC is a fact about the ledger, not a comment on the player.

Rubber bands (Civ difficulty bonuses, Mario Kart) or any term that reads the player's score to help the trailer — use the historical catch-ups instead (new battlegrounds, FIRSTS, end-weighted checkpoints, the fogged score).
A second scoring system per nation archetype — 86 rulesets are unmaintainable and unteachable; keep one formula and move all asymmetry into the sourced expectation rows and reach/column data.
Freezing the checkpoint on one tick with public dates — invites December aid surges and coups timed to resolve on 30 December; freeze the trailing-twelve-month mean and say so.

Rewarding the turtle — an avoided-catastrophe line without superpower expectation rows that demand movement makes 'sit on 1950' the dominant USA play; import Twilight Struggle's military-ops lesson as expectations, not as a penalty term.

A 'beat history' baseline written as events rather than outcomes — the world diverges from the first decision, so 'Korea armistice by July 1953' is unmeasurable in a game where Korea may never happen; write rows as ranks, column counts, SoL deltas and sovereignty.

Showing a raw score number in the HUD — the house rules forbid it and Balance of Power's single prestige number is the precedent for a number detached from the world; lines are bands and sentences, the class is a word, the only integers are the exact dead.

The hands-off 'world without you' as the primary baseline — it makes your own nation an AI counterfactual, costs a background run per seed, and reads as a mirror match; keep it as a v2 retrospective flourish.

Applying the taboo ceiling to a world where the AI broke the taboo — the ceiling must key on the attributed user (command log), never on the global flag, or the player is punished for the rival's crime.
analysts.first_hour_test: Founding edition, January 1950, before the first unpause: THE WORLD IN NUMBERS rail carries THE LEDGER — four lines, each a verdict sentence with its 1955 expectation and no number. USA: 'STANDING: AHEAD — WEST DOMINATES EUROPE, ASIA CONTESTED. BY 1955: HOLD EUROPE, DENY ASIA. / PROSPERITY: LEADING. / SECURITY: SECURE. / PEACE: HELD — TENSION WARY, THE TABOO INTACT.' USSR (party organ): 'STANDING: ON COURSE — EAST HOLDS THE PEOPLE'S DEMOCRACIES, PEKING BOUND BY TREATY. BY 1955: PRESENCE IN ASIA. / PROSPERITY: BEHIND (REPORTED) — THE PROGRAMME SAYS 1970. / SECURITY: SECURE. / PEACE: HELD.' Guatemala (gazette): 'SECURITY: WATCHED — STABILITY 55, ARMY US-EQUIPPED, DECREE 900 NOT YET LAW. BY 1955: STILL SOVEREIGN. / STANDING: DENIED COLUMN, CENTRAL AMERICA. / PROSPERITY: STAGNANT.' Each line is a deep link to the panel whose verbs move it, so the player learns in the first game-hour which panel answers which line. Jan-Jun 1950 the lines do not wiggle: they change band at most once a month, and when one does the paper prints the cause ('SECURITY: WATCHED to SHAKEN — WASHINGTON'S CHEQUEBOOK NAMES YOU'). June 25 tests the USA's PEACE line (Korea's aim ladder prices legitimacy and tension right where the line reads). At the first checkpoint, 1955-01-01, the RECKONING edition prints each line's year-on-the-record band against the 1955 expectation, a TRAJECTORY word, the top three named causes, the rival's four lines as bracketed estimates ('EAST STANDING: PROBABLY BEHIND, EST. 9-13 STATES'), 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD: 14 BATTLEGROUNDS' under THE COLONIAL QUESTION, and one masthead sentence: 'ON COURSE, RISING' — and for a Guatemala player who kept Arbenz through June 1954, 'AHEAD OF HISTORY: STILL SOVEREIGN.' No percentages, no totals, no score number anywhere.

findings.title: The scoring surface already exists in fragments; TickSet::Resolve is empty and is its designed home
findings.detail: Every raw input the vision's four score dimensions need is already a sim resource with a stable digest: regional standings and frozen Checkpoints (influence.rs:232-247, freeze at influence.rs:1995-2011 on new_month && month==1 && CHECKPOINT_YEARS), bloc state/population totals (influence.rs:2187-2208), per-country industry actual vs reported (planning.rs:77-88), legitimacy (settlement.rs:256, 281), nuclear Stage milestones and the taboo flag (nuclear.rs:78-89, 226), casualties and battles (military.rs:296-307), crisis resolve (crisis.rs:137), completed Great Projects (construction.rs:174), and the GameOver terminal record (crisis.rs:94-103). What does not exist is a place that reads them together: no `Score`, `prestige`, or `victory` symbol exists in ugs-sim or ugs-app (grep), and `TickSet::Resolve` is documented as 'Derived state, victory checks' (lib.rs:63) yet has zero systems registered (lib.rs:139-174). The v1 Ledger is therefore a pure monthly fold over existing resources, registered as the first occupant of Resolve, and adds no new mechanics to the tick.

findings.title: Attribution gaps: the sim knows THAT the taboo broke and THAT a crisis ended, not WHO did it
findings.detail: `NuclearPrograms.taboo_broken` is a global bool set at nuclear.rs:580 inside a branch where the user `me` is in scope, but the user and tick are not recorded; the digest folds the flag only as `alert + 100` (nuclear.rs:270). Crisis outcomes adjust `resolve` (crisis.rs:326-327: actor -cost, other +VICTORY_RESOLVE) but keep no per-country count of times prevailed / stood down, so a prestige term cannot say 'PREVAILED IN THREE CRISES' without re-deriving it from FiredEvents.resolved strings. Treaties drop the proposer: `Proposal.proposer` (settlement.rs:230) is not carried into `Treaty` (settlement.rs:236-241), so 'peace made' cannot be credited. These are the only three fields a score needs that must be ADDED to existing resources; everything else is a read.

findings.title: Epistemic texture is already mechanised for output; reuse it rather than inventing a second estimate path
findings.detail: `Economies::dashboard_industry_centi` returns the bureau's `reported_centi` for planned systems and `actual_centi` for market (planning.rs:116-124); `observed_industry_centi(tag, penetration)` interpolates reported→actual by the viewer's economic penetration (planning.rs:131-139) using `Intel::knowledge(viewer, subject, Domain::Economic)` (intel.rs:170). Reported is clamped to [actual, actual*1.15] under MISREPORT_CAP_PERMILLE (planning.rs:419-424), so a Soviet player's OWN score line is honestly inflated by his own statisticians, and the American estimate of it narrows only with penetration. The paper already renders rival strength as a jittered range via `intel_width`/`est_men_range` seeded from month^tag (paper_ui.rs:630-640) and stamps every edition 'FOREIGN FIGURES ARE ESTIMATES' (paper_ui.rs:703-706). Legitimacy is world opinion and therefore public/exact for everyone; casualties are exact for self (paper_ui.rs:672 'OUR FALLEN ... (EXACT)') and ranged for rivals. A score view is thus a viewer-parameterised function over an exact ledger, exactly like `verdict_sentence` (influence.rs:2210-2270).

findings.title: The catastrophe path is already correct in shape: GameOver is a resource, the funeral screen refuses a score, and the sim keeps state to write the past-tense verdict
findings.detail: `crisis::update_crises` inserts `GameOver { initiator, against, tick, dead, cities }` at rung >= 8 (crisis.rs:340-371) after `tension.apply(1000)`; endgame.rs `the_end` pauses the app every frame while the resource exists (endgame.rs:33-40) and prints 'THE PEACE HELD N YEARS' (endgame.rs:127) and 'WE DO NOT REWARD FAILURE' (endgame.rs:142), explicitly citing Crawford's Balance of Power rule (endgame.rs:1-5; Chris Crawford, Balance of Power, Mindscape 1985: no mushroom cloud, no score). Twilight Struggle (GMT Games, 2005) uses the same device: DEFCON 1 ends the game and the PHASING player loses regardless of VP — the initiator field (crisis.rs:365) is that rule. The composition rule for a score is therefore: the Ledger records `end = Exchange{initiator}` and the funeral prints at most one past-tense line from the LAST frozen era card ('THE 1960 RECKONING HAD READ: ...'). No live total is ever shown on that screen. The winner of the exchange is not computed anywhere and must never be. `the_end` computes years as tick/(24*365) (endgame.rs:49-50), which drifts across 1952/56/60/64/68 leap years; the ledger should compute from GameDate.

findings.title: Three registries plus two digests must be touched for any new state resource, and the current registries already disagree
findings.detail: New sim state must be (1) init'd in SimPlugin (lib.rs:104-122), (2) reset in `reset_sim` (savegame.rs:66-85, including the `remove_resource::<GameOver>()` pattern at :79 for insert-once resources), (3) folded into the interleaved determinism snapshot (tests/determinism.rs:35-76, doc comment 'Add every new state resource here') and (4) the save/replay digest (savegame.rs:137-158). Today `LivingStandards` (demography.rs:84-86) is in registries 1 and 2 but in neither digest and has no `digest()` fn, and `GameOver` presence is in no digest. `Influence::digest` folds `standings` and `checkpoints` even though they are derived (influence.rs:849-875), while `Military.active_battles` and `Influence.wire/last_month/pressures` are excluded as narrative (military.rs:308-310, influence.rs:288-298). Precedent says: fold the numeric score card and the frozen era records; exclude the rendered sentences.

findings.title: One card for all 86 playable nations: a per-pole column inherited through alignment_of plus a per-nation column, no second system
findings.detail: All alignment reads go through `Military::alignment_of` (military.rs:324-328, 367), which returns WesternBloc/EasternBloc/NonAligned for every country including the player; `bloc_totals` already produces three columns (West/East/denied) and `RegionStanding` carries `denied` per region (influence.rs:232-238, 2187-2208). So a ScoreCard is `poles: [PoleCard; 3]` plus `nations: BTreeMap<CountryTag, NationCard>`, and a country's alignment term is simply its pole's column — the UK player reads the West's Europe verdict as 'our side', India reads the denied column. The national column uses fields that exist for every tag: `IndustryState.actual_centi` growth vs the 1950 seed (planning.rs:79, 216), `LivingStandards.by_country` (demography.rs:85), `legitimacy_of` (settlement.rs:281), sovereignty from `Influence::is_locked`/lock label (influence.rs:303-312, CLIENT_LOCK_MONTHS :106), `Settlements.neutralized` (settlement.rs:270) and occupied provinces where `military.occupation` holder != owner (military.rs:292), nuclear Stage per program (UK Tested 1952, France 1960, PRC 1964 arrive from data, nuclear.rs:78-89). This is Balance of Power's single prestige formula (Crawford 1985: sum over countries of relationship x weight) and Victoria II's one Great-Power ranking (Paradox 2010: prestige + industry + military for every tag) — both scored 100+ countries with one formula and let the verdict sentence pick the lead clause.

findings.title: The reckoning cadence is already a data constant with a hands-off 20-year harness to assert against
findings.detail: `tuning::CHECKPOINT_YEARS = [1955, 1960, 1965]` (influence.rs:104) and the freeze predicate fires on the 1955-01-01 00:00 tick (test `checkpoints_freeze_at_the_era_dates`, influence.rs:2892-2900, runs 24*(365*5+3) ticks — the +3 is leap days). The corpus runs to 1970-09-04 (events.ron, last date) and `the_world_turns_to_1970` (events.rs:970) runs twenty hands-off years asserting '1970 is not a world war' (world-timeline.md:156-158). Adding a FINAL_YEAR = 1970 reckoning on the same predicate and asserting in that test that `Ledger.end == Reckoning(1970)` and no pole card carries an Exchange gives the victory rule a regression harness for free. The score freeze must key off `influence.checkpoints.len()` (dependency-driven, save/replay safe) rather than a second copy of the date predicate.

findings.title: The newspaper is the score surface and already prints half of it; the missing piece is the verdict sentence and the era edition
findings.detail: paper_ui.rs prints INFLUENCE STANDINGS with bloc totals, per-region CONTESTED/DOMINATES lines, 'ON THE RECORD SINCE THE {year} RECKONING' (paper_ui.rs:553-600), OUR STANDING (LEGITIMACY) (:614-620), the rival arsenal estimate (:622-641), and the war report with exact own casualties (:660-690). It recomputes population by holder inline (:560-566) because `population_by_holder` is private (influence.rs:1270) — a third copy in a score module would be a smell; export it. newspaper.md:86-91 designs the page as a section registry precisely so a ledger page slots in. The house rule 'the unit of legibility is a computed verdict sentence' is already implemented for countries (`verdict_sentence`, influence.rs:2210) and for probability words (`kent_word`, influence.rs:952 — Sherman Kent, 'Words of Estimative Probability', Studies in Intelligence 1964). A campaign verdict is the same pattern one level up: one sentence per pole, one for the player's nation, printed as THE STANDING every month and as a full FINAL EDITION at each reckoning.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: The Ledger: one monthly Resolve-set resource, four terms, three pole columns plus a national column, frozen at 1955/1960/1965/1970
mechanics_recommendations.why: Answers brief items (1), (2), (c) and (d) with zero new tick mechanics: every input is an existing digest-stable resource; O(countries + battlegrounds) integer sums once a month is negligible against the hourly military/economy passes; one formula covers USA, SOV, UK, India and Guatemala because the pole column is inherited through `alignment_of` and the national column uses fields every tag has. Twilight Struggle's Presence/Domination/Control are literally the `Verdict` enum (influence.rs:212-218), so the alignment term is already a scored regional standing; Civilization VI: Rise and Fall (Firaxis, 2018) shows era-boundary scoring with banded outcomes (Dark/Normal/Golden) reads better than a running total.
mechanics_recommendations.how: New `crates/ugs-sim/src/score.rs`: `tuning` (FINAL_YEAR=1970; verdict weights CONTROL=3/DOMINATION=2/PRESENCE=1 x `BattlegroundDef.weight` — the weight field exists at ugs-data lib.rs:442 and is currently unused by `compute_standings` influence.rs:2151-2158; band thresholds). `PoleCard { held: u8, dominated: u8, controlled: u8, states: u32, pop_k: u64, output_centi: u64, prestige: i32, brink_months: u16, first_use: bool }`, `NationCard { output_centi, output_1950_centi, sol, legitimacy, sovereignty: Sovereign|Client|Neutralized|Occupied, nuclear: Stage-like enum, prevailed: u16, stood_down: u16, fallen_men: u64 }`, `Ledger { poles: [PoleCard;3], nations: BTreeMap<CountryTag, NationCard>, eras: Vec<Era { year, poles, nations }>, end: Option<CampaignEnd> }` with `CampaignEnd::{Reckoning(i32), Exchange{initiator, tick}}`. System `update_score` in `TickSet::Resolve` (lib.rs after :174), body gated on `clock.new_month`; also runs the tick a `GameOver` resource appears (`Option<Res<GameOver>>`) to set `end = Exchange`. Inputs: alignment from `Influence.standings` + `bloc_totals` (influence.rs:2187) with exported `population_by_holder`; output from `Economies.industry[t].actual_centi` summed by `military.alignment_of` per pole; prestige = `settlements.legitimacy_of` + nuclear Stage rank (Tested=+, Thermonuclear=+) + completed Great Projects joined `Construction.completed_great` to `GreatProjectDef.country` (ugs-data lib.rs:518-534) + crises prevailed; catastrophe = `military.casualties * MEN_PER_STRENGTH_POINT`, months with `tension.band() == Brink`, `nuclear.first_use` attribution, exploitation zones already priced via legitimacy (settlement.rs:1371-1375; do not double count). Freeze when `influence.checkpoints.len() > ledger.eras.len()` or year == FINAL_YEAR && month == 1. Digest folds every numeric field (precedent influence.rs:849-875); register in SimPlugin (lib.rs:104-122), `reset_sim` (savegame.rs:85 + `remove_resource` none needed since Ledger is a plain resource), tests/determinism.rs:73 (`|score:{:x}`), savegame.rs:140 digest. Player-facing decisions each term changes: alignment -> which battleground gets a program slot (`StartProgram`, influence.rs:969) and crush/tolerate; output -> `set_planned_allocation` (planning.rs:442) investment share; prestige is the SAME number spent on settlement clauses (settlement.rs:745), so prestige literally buys peace terms; catastrophe -> back down vs escalate (crisis.rs:314) and atomic release (nuclear.rs:486).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Verdict sentences with epistemic views: the ledger is exact, the reading is per-viewer, foreign output is an estimate, own planned output is what the bureau reports
mechanics_recommendations.why: House rules: computed verdict sentence, never raw percentages, planners see REPORTED figures, foreign numbers are estimates. The machinery already exists (planning.rs:116-139, intel.rs:170, paper_ui.rs est_men_range) — a score that showed the true Soviet industry to a US player would break the espionage pillar's payoff (penetration exists to narrow exactly this estimate), and a Soviet player whose own score used `actual_centi` would see through his own statisticians for free, defeating the planned-economy misreporting mechanic (planning.rs:419-424).
mechanics_recommendations.how: Two pure functions in score.rs mirroring `verdict_sentence` (influence.rs:2210): `pole_sentence(ledger, pole, viewer: Option<&CountryTag>, intel, econ, data) -> String` and `nation_sentence(...)`.
