Output: own pole/nation uses `dashboard_industry_centi` (reported for Planned); the rival pole sums `observed_industry_centi(t, intel.knowledge(me, t, Domain::Economic))` over its members, then words the ratio through bands (AHEAD BY HALF / AHEAD BY A THIRD / LEVEL / BEHIND ...) using `kent_word`-style tables (influence.rs:952), never a number. Legitimacy prints exact for everyone (world opinion is public). Rival casualties print as a range through the existing `intel_width`/`est_men_range` helpers moved from paper_ui.rs:630-640 into sim as integer arithmetic (no f64; the paper's `sig2` log10 at paper_ui.rs:568-574 stays app-side). The sentence grammar is fixed-order clauses: [alignment] [output] [peace] [prestige], e.g. 'THE WEST DOMINATES EUROPE AND THE AMERICAS, CONTESTS ASIA AND THE MIDDLE EAST. OUTPUT AHEAD BY A THIRD (AS REPORTED). THE PEACE HAS HELD FIVE YEARS; THE TABOO HOLDS. STANDING: HIGH.' A minor's sentence leads with sovereignty and living standard: 'SOVEREIGN. OUTPUT UP BY HALF SINCE 1950; LIVING STANDARD: RISING. OUR SIDE DOMINATES EUROPE. NO WAR DEAD.' Print monthly as THE STANDING in the paper (new section after INFLUENCE STANDINGS, paper_ui.rs:553) and as the lead of every reckoning edition. Each freeze pushes one wire line (influence.rs:2007 'THE {year} RECKONING' already fires) so the month it happens is unmistakable.

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Campaign end and the pyrrhic rule: a `CampaignEnd` at 1970-01-01 that composes with, and is silenced by, `GameOver`
mechanics_recommendations.why: Brief items (b), (e): the 1970 verdict must exist; the exchange must remain playable (the sim runs it through rung 8 and computes the dead — crisis.rs:340-360) but never scoreable. Crawford's rule already governs endgame.rs; Twilight Struggle's DEFCON-1 'phasing player loses' and Balance of Power's 'you have ignited a nuclear war' are the two shipped precedents for an unwinnable terminal state inside a scored game. EU4 (Paradox 2013) shows the soft-end pattern: the 1821 end screen with 'continue playing' — needed because the corpus has events through 1970-09-04.
mechanics_recommendations.how: Sim: `Ledger.end` is set once: `Reckoning(1970)` on the 1970-01-01 new_month tick (after the era freeze so `eras.last()` is 1970), or `Exchange{initiator, tick}` copied from `GameOver` the tick it appears. Tactical first use (nuclear.rs:580) records `NuclearPrograms.first_use: Option<(CountryTag, u64)>` (fold into digest at nuclear.rs:270) and from then on every sentence for that pole carries 'FIRST USE: {tag}, {date}' as a permanent clause (Tannenwald, The Nuclear Taboo, Cambridge UP 2007 — the taboo is one-way; the code already says 'FOR EVERYONE, FOREVER' nuclear.rs:590). App: endgame.rs gains `the_reckoning` system on `Option<Res<Ledger>>` with `.run_if(not(resource_exists::<GameOver>))`, pauses via `speed.paused = true` once (not every frame like `the_end` at :37 — keep an app-side `Acknowledged(bool)` resource so [SPACE: PLAY ON] works and the sim keeps ticking into 1970's events), spawns a full-page FINAL EDITION reusing the paper's masthead/columns (paper_ui.rs:304-360) with three pole sentences, the player's nation sentence, and the four era cards as a dated table (1955/1960/1965/1970 — 'monthly date-stamped still displays'). `the_end` (GameOver) gets exactly one added line after 'THE PEACE HELD' (endgame.rs:127): 'THE LAST RECKONING ({year}) HAD READ: {pole_sentence of the initiator's pole}', in past tense, INK_DIM, taken from `ledger.eras.last()` — the score exists on that screen only as what was thrown away. No winner is computed for an exchange anywhere in sim; `PoleCard` has no field for it. Fix the years/months computation at endgame.rs:49-50 to use GameDate (leap years 1952/56/60/64/68).

mechanics_recommendations.mechanic: Attribution counters added to existing resources (not to the Ledger) so the score reads them like everything else
mechanics_recommendations.why: The three inputs the score needs that do not exist are causal records (who broke the taboo, who prevailed/stood down in a crisis, who proposed a treaty). They belong beside the mechanics that produce them, folded into those resources' digests, so the Ledger stays a pure read and the determinism registries do not grow by three.
mechanics_recommendations.how: nuclear.rs:226 add `pub first_use: Option<(CountryTag, u64)>` set at :580 alongside `taboo_broken = true`; fold at :270. crisis.rs:137 add `pub prevailed: BTreeMap<CountryTag, u16>` and `pub stood_down: BTreeMap<CountryTag, u16>` incremented at :326-327 (the SEEK/quiet-diplomacy branch at :410-416 increments neither: 'NEITHER CAPITAL CLAIMS VICTORY'); fold at :190-212 next to `resolve`. settlement.rs:236 add `pub proposer: CountryTag` to `Treaty` from `Proposal.proposer` at the accept site; fold in `Settlements::digest` (:351). Tests: extend `the_general_exchange_ends_the_campaign` (nuclear.rs:819) to assert `first_use` names the user; add a crisis test that a deadline default increments `stood_down` for the ball-holder and `prevailed` for the other.

pitfalls: Putting `update_score` anywhere but `TickSet::Resolve`: standings are recomputed inside `update_influence` in Politics (influence.rs:1994) and month-end production lands in Economy, which runs BEFORE Politics in the chained sets (lib.rs:126-134); a score system in Economy or Politics would freeze last month's standings or pre-production output at the checkpoint tick.

Reading `IndustryState.actual_centi` for the rival's column or `reported_centi` for a market economy: the epistemic contract is `dashboard_industry_centi` for self and `observed_industry_centi(t, intel.knowledge(me, t, Economic))` for others (planning.rs:116-139); anything else either leaks truth through the score or shows the planner his own lie.

Double-charging legitimacy: exploitation zones (settlement.rs:1375), coups (influence.rs:87), exposed ops (:89), recognising juntas (:93) and UNSC-style scripted grants already move `legitimacy`; the prestige term must READ legitimacy, never re-penalise the same acts, or the settlement table's pricing (settlement.rs:734-748) silently changes.

Any f64 in score.rs: the paper's `sig2` rounding uses `(n as f64).log10()` (paper_ui.rs:568-574) and `est_men_range` lives app-side; moving them into sim without integer rewrites breaks bit-identical digests across platforms. Years-since-start must come from `GameDate`, not `tick / (24*365)` (endgame.rs:49-50 already drifts across 1952).

Forgetting a registry: SimPlugin (lib.rs:104-122), `reset_sim` (savegame.rs:66-85), `tests/determinism.rs` snapshot (:35-76) and the savegame digest (:137-158). `LivingStandards` is the standing example of a resource in two of four; if the score reads it, give it a `digest()` and add it to both snapshots in the same PR.

Feeding the Ledger to the AI allocator: the USA/SOV allocator already has its own candidate score (influence.rs:2050, weight x pop x (1000-|pos|)); letting AI blocs optimise the victory total turns the scoring rule into a hidden AI objective and makes every balance change a double change. Keep the Ledger read-only for AI in v1.

Building a score PANEL: the house rule is no panel without a verb. The Ledger has no verb; it is a paper section (THE STANDING), four dated reckoning editions, and one past-tense line on the funeral screen. A live running total anywhere on the HUD invites optimisation of a number instead of reading a verdict.

Letting the exchange be scored by omission: if `PoleCard` retains enough to rank poles after `GameOver`, someone will print it. Set `end = Exchange` and stop updating the cards that tick; the only post-exchange text is the last frozen era card in past tense.

Freezing the score on a second copy of the date predicate instead of `influence.checkpoints.len()`: two predicates can drift (leap-year tick math, a future change to CHECKPOINT_YEARS) and a save replay would then disagree with the paper's 'ON THE RECORD SINCE THE {year} RECKONING' line (paper_ui.rs:594-600).
analysts.first_hour_test: Jan 1950: the founding edition (paper_ui.rs edge case, newspaper.md:96-97) carries a new THE STANDING box under INFLUENCE STANDINGS with one sentence per pole and one for the player, in words only, dated 1 JANUARY 1950, and a line 'NEXT RECKONING: 1 JANUARY 1955'. Playing the USA: 'THE WEST CONTROLS THE AMERICAS, DOMINATES EUROPE, CONTESTS ASIA AND THE MIDDLE EAST. OUTPUT AHEAD BY HALF (SOVIET FIGURES ESTIMATED). THE PEACE HOLDS: CALM. STANDING: HIGH.' Playing the USSR the same edition reads from the People's Observer masthead: 'THE EAST CONTROLS EASTERN EUROPE, HOLDS PRESENCE IN ASIA. OUTPUT BEHIND BY A THIRD (AS REPORTED BY GOSPLAN). THE PEACE HOLDS: CALM.' Playing India: 'SOVEREIGN. NON-ALIGNED: 3 STATES DENIED TO BOTH BLOCS. OUTPUT LEVEL WITH 1950. LIVING STANDARD: LOW. NO WAR DEAD.' Feb–Jun 1950: the sentence must NOT change month to month except for the tension clause word (CALM/WARY) and, after a program is placed, the alignment clause only when a region's verdict actually flips — a player who does nothing should read the same sentence for six months and learn that the reckoning is what moves. 25 Jun 1950 (Korea event fires): the July edition's peace clause becomes 'WAR IN KOREA; OUR FALLEN: 0 (EXACT)' for a belligerent, 'WAR IN KOREA' for others, and for the USA 'OUTPUT ... (AS REPORTED)' stays put while the war report shows exact casualties — the first hour teaches that catastrophe is counted in men, alignment in regions, output in words, prestige in legitimacy spent at the table. First checkpoint, 1 Jan 1955 00:00 tick: the wire prints 'THE 1955 RECKONING: STANDINGS FROZEN FOR THE RECORD' (influence.rs:2007) and the app opens a full-page RECKONING edition (paper masthead, three pole sentences, the player's nation sentence, and a four-row dated table with only the 1955 row filled) that pauses once and offers [SPACE: PLAY ON] [N: FOLD]; every later monthly paper carries 'ON THE RECORD SINCE THE 1955 RECKONING' with the frozen sentence in INK_DIM beneath the live one, so the player can see what changed since the record was taken. Acceptance: the same seed and the same commands print byte-identical sentences in both apps of the determinism test at 1955-01-01, and a save loaded at 1954-12-31 reproduces the identical 1955 card.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: 'Avoided catastrophe as a shared positive line, and a general exchange as a survival multiplier rather than a zero'; board-game-scoring-cadence: 'THE CATASTROPHE TRACK' epitaph line; asymmetric-goals-and-fun: 'VERDICT CEILINGS' funeral line 'BY THE LEDGER, X WON'
objections.objection: Three of six analysts print a winner under the mushroom cloud. A 'survival multiplier' is a score for the exchange (multiply six lines by survivors and the side with more survivors is ahead: that is DEFCON's Survivor mode with better prose). 'THE LEDGER AS OF 14 OCT 1962: WEST +9. IT DID NOT MATTER' and 'BY THE LEDGER, WASHINGTON WON. THE LEDGER IS ALL THAT SURVIVED' are the screenshot line every player will play for once they are 60 ahead and the AI is climbing; 'it did not matter' is editorial, the printed +9 is the fact. The brief says the big war must never be win-able even by accident; any ranked figure on the funeral screen, in any tense, is an accidental win. Only verdict-legibility ('A catastrophe screen that ranks...') and systems-integration ('Letting the exchange be scored by omission') get this right, and even systems-integration wants 'THE LAST RECKONING HAD READ: {pole_sentence}' which names who was ahead. The funeral must print the dead, the initiator, the years the peace held, and nothing that orders the poles.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: 'The ledger gap as the trailing side's risk appetite (the runaway effect without an auto-win)'
objections.objection: This turns the score into a reverse thermostat. If a lead makes the AI rival climb crisis rungs and coup at CHANCES ABOUT EVEN, the leading player's optimal play is to sandbag (stay NARROW, hold back the December aid so the provisional line never reads CLEAR) or, worse, to lean into it: with TS-style attribution the defender who stays calm while a desperate Moscow fires first 'wins' the exchange by attribution. Combine this with the funeral epitaph above and you have designed the DEFCON-suicide play the genre analyst warns about, from the leader's side. It is also score-watching in its purest form: the player now watches the provisional integer to keep the AI docile. Systems-integration ('Keep the Ledger read-only for AI in v1') and asymmetric-goals ('score-AWARE, never score-CHASING') both say no; three analysts disagree on the single most consequential feedback loop in the design and nobody adjudicated.

objections.target: genre-victory-systems: 'The checkpoint writes back into the sim: grades change slots, legitimacy and domestic events'
objections.objection: The analyst spends a whole finding warning about Vic2 prestige compounding, then ships the compounding: ASCENDANT grants an influence slot (the winner gets more capacity to win), ECLIPSED fires a leadership-challenge chain and HUMILIATED debits legitimacy for the next era (the loser gets a second penalty on top of the map they already lost). That is EU4 Great Power / Splendour, which snowballed exactly this way. A 1955 ASCENDANT USA with an extra slot holds Africa in 1960 more easily; a 1955 ECLIPSED USSR spends 1956 in a Politburo event chain instead of in India. The write-back should be neutral or counter-cyclical (the trailing pole gets the domestic 'do something' mandate that unlocks a verb; the leader gets scrutiny), or there should be no write-back beyond the paper. 'Ship the write-backs or ship nothing' is the wrong ultimatum; 'ship no snowball' is the right one.

objections.target: genre-victory-systems: 'THE RECKONING: one scoreboard of four era terms, graded per era against the deterministic hands-off baseline'; verdict-legibility: 'THE HISTORICAL PAR'; asymmetric-goals-and-fun: 'Beat history beats beat the hands-off AI'
objections.objection: Grading against a ghost. The hands-off run is the world in which the player did nothing, so by construction a passive USA reads AS HISTORY / HELD THE LINE at every reckoning: the score's first lesson is that doing nothing is fine, which is the turtle the asymmetric analyst then has to fix with expectation rows. Worse, par.ron is baked at ship time from one seed and one timeline corpus; every influence-tuning commit or new timeline event silently moves the target, and the player only ever sees AHEAD/AS/BEHIND with no way to learn what par was ('never print what history did' is also demanded). A moving, invisible target is neither legible nor tunable, and it is the 'second game nobody will tune' in disguise: a regenerated table per build that the harness must re-bless. Asymmetric-goals sees this and proposes sourced OUTCOME rows instead, then admits they fall back to three archetype rows, which means the archetype row is the real system and the 1,376 sourced rows (86 nations x 4 checkpoints x 4 lines) are flavour nobody will maintain. Pick a comparator the player can see on day one and that does not change under the sim's feet: the rival (for poles) and the nation's own 1950 line (for everyone else), full stop.

objections.target: genre-victory-systems: era grade = 'the median of the four terms with THE PEACE able to cap it'
objections.objection: Median of four mostly-static words prints the same grade every era. THE PEACE is HOLDING in any campaign without first use; STANDING (legitimacy band) is HOLDING for most nations most of the time; so median{ALIGNMENT, SYSTEMS, HOLDING, HOLDING} is HOLDING unless both moving terms agree. The USSR player who wins Africa and Asia in 1960 reads HOLDING; the USA who loses them reads HOLDING. A grade that cannot move is the EU4 score with fewer digits. Same problem with per-era reset: the analyst names 'reset resentment' as a pitfall and then ships a design where a player who built a +20 lead in 1955 and held it flat through 1960 is graded HOLDING/ECLIPSED for 'not gaining', while board-game-scoring-cadence's delta-sum keeps the lead banked. Two analysts propose contradictory snowball cures (reset per era vs sum of deltas) and neither is reconciled.

objections.target: asymmetric-goals-and-fun: 'VERDICT CEILINGS instead of penalties for the catastrophes'; genre-victory-systems: 'any first use caps the user at ECLIPSED'
objections.objection: A ceiling is a zero with a delay and a free second shot. Once the taboo is broken in 1953 the player is told for seventeen years that SURVIVED is the best they can do: that is the quit point the analyst claims to avoid ('a zero makes the remaining fifteen years pointless'), merely relabelled. And because the cap is a step, not a slope, the marginal score cost of the second, third and tenth tactical use is exactly zero: the capped player is now the freest nuclear power on the board. Ceilings need a slope beneath them (each use, each 100k dead, keeps costing something inside the class) or the score actively teaches 'in for a penny'. Also 'RUIN below EXCHANGE' as classes in a hall of records is a ranking of catastrophes, which invites the 'least bad Armageddon' run.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: 'THE LEDGER: one integer score per nation per era from three terms plus a par' (OUTPUT term and the hands-off tuning target)
objections.objection: One third of the score is a constant the Soviet player cannot touch. OUTPUT = clamp((own actual industry per capita - rival's)/STEP, -4, +4) reads +3/+4 West every era by the analyst's own numbers; the USSR cannot triple per-capita output by 1960 with any allocation, so the term is a structural handicap rendered as a spreadsheet line, and then the analyst 'tunes the OUTPUT cap and STANDING bands so hands-off lands West +1..+6' and asserts it in the harness. Tuning score knobs to make the do-nothing run land on a target number is tuning the spreadsheet, not the game; it guarantees the score is uninformative about the player. The historian's MOMENTUM/STANDING pair at least gives the planner a term they lead, but doubles the word count. Either OUTPUT must be scored as growth vs own 1950 (movable by investment share) or it should not be a superpower score term at all.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: 'One era scorecard with six lines, each printed as a band word plus a MOMENTUM arrow and a STANDING word' and 'Dated score dimensions... terms switch on by event'
objections.objection: Six lines x two words x three columns (OURS / THEIR ESTIMATE / AS THEY CLAIM, per verdict-legibility) is a 36-cell table with a 'BELIEVED vs TRUE' overlay at freeze; that is a ledger, not a verdict, and it fails verdict-legibility's own 80-word card. Dimensions that switch on with a rival's first (space arrives with Sputnik) are a scripted shock the first time and an exploit the second: a leader who cannot win a race simply never funds it and the dimension never opens, while the AI opens dimensions on its historical calendar regardless. Cohesion and credibility as separate lines also double-count legitimacy (systems-integration's 'do not re-penalise the same acts'). Keep the six as newspaper flavour; score four at most.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: 'Loss attribution... debits a domestic line at roughly three times the credit of a gain'; asymmetric-goals-and-fun: 'The do-nothing turtle... expectation rows that demand movement'
objections.objection: A 3x loss debit is a rule that says 'never let a client wobble', i.e. escalate every wobble; the analyst cites McNaughton's 70% and then caps the debit 'so escalation can cost more than the headline', which is a tuning promise, not a mechanism, and the cap cannot be tested until the war system produces Vietnam. Combined with expectation rows that DEMAND movement (DENY ASIA, PRESENCE IN AFRICA), the superpower player is handed a to-do list with punishments, which is precisely the Civ VII 'checklist feel' the genre analyst warns about. Twilight Struggle's Military Ops floor works because a turn is ten minutes; a five-year checklist with a 3x loss penalty is homework.

objections.target: asymmetric-goals-and-fun: 'THE FOGGED SCORE' (the rival's ledger as an anti-coasting device)
objections.objection: Fog on a score that the freeze un-fogs every five years is not an anti-coasting device; it is a prompt to buy economic penetration before each reckoning and then coast with confidence. The 'PROBABLY LEADING' qualifier is good epistemic texture, but the claim that it keeps a leader playing is unsupported by any cited game (no precedent 'got this right' by the genre analyst's own admission). It also creates a new score-watching loop: refresh the estimate bracket monthly to see if it narrowed. Fine as texture, not as the mechanism that solves coasting.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: 'Middle and minor powers score with the same three-line formula...' (Japan's century won on OUTPUT with the map term flat); systems-integration: national column reads LivingStandards
objections.objection: The minor's game is two terms they cannot move. LivingStandards is static in v1 (board-game admits it), a zero-slot minor has no map verb, and legitimacy for Luxembourg moves only when a scripted event touches it. So the first-hour test's promise that Luxembourg's standing line points at a real verb ('[E] ECONOMY or TREATY') points at verbs that do not change the score term in v1. That is a quit point in the first hour for 60 of 86 nations. The honest answer is that minors' scores are read-only until SoL moves and minors get a treaty/denial verb; say so in the design instead of pretending one formula already serves them.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: 'An annual Assembly roll-call as the ledger's public integer'
objections.objection: By the analyst's own admission it is tautological with alignment and there are 'no votes to buy in v1': a fourth rendering of the same standings (map paint, verdict words, ledger box, roll-call) with no verb attached, violating the house rule outright. It is also the one place a raw integer would appear every September, which invites exactly the counting the design forbids. Cut, or defer until courting a newborn before its first session is a verb.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: 'THE CATASTROPHE TRACK' SCARRED threshold of 1,000,000 own dead
objections.objection: An absolute headcount as a grade cap is not one formula for 86 nations: 1,000,000 dead is 0.6% of the USA, 0.2% of the PRC and three Luxembourgs. A PRC player in the scripted Korean War is at risk of a scripted cap; a superpower can fight a Korea-scale war (36k US dead) with no mark at all. If casualties cap a grade, cap on per-capita or share-of-1950-population, and print it as the Kahn table the asymmetric analyst suggests rather than as a threshold.

objections.target: All six: the 'decision each score term changes' answer
objections.objection: Every analyst answers 'what decision does this term change' by naming a verb the player already has for non-score reasons (slot placement, investment share, back down vs escalate). None gives a worked case where the score makes a player choose differently than they would with the score turned off. If the score never overrides the pillar-local optimum, it is a lens, not a mechanic, and a lens is a spreadsheet. The strongest candidate is systems-integration's observation that legitimacy is spent on settlement clauses, so the prestige term literally buys peace terms; that tradeoff (spend standing to end a war early) is the only place in the six outputs where the score is a cost. Build the design around that kind of exchange or accept that the score is only a reckoning surface.

missing: Convergence on a vocabulary: six analysts ship six grade lexicons (TRIUMPH/ASCENDANT/HOLDING/ECLIPSED/HUMILIATED; STALEMATE/NARROW/CLEAR/DECISIVE; LEADING/EVEN/TRAILING; AHEAD/ON COURSE/BEHIND/FAILING; BEAT THE CENTURY/HELD THE LINE/LOST THE DECADE; TRIUMPH/VICTORY/HELD/SURVIVED/DECLINE/RUIN). One monthly word set, one era word set, one campaign word set, chosen and frozen before implementation.

A single adjudicated rule for whether the AI reads the score: three positions on the table (read-only, self-grade only, gap-as-risk-appetite). Decide it; it is the loop that determines whether a lead is fun or a threat.

A worked decision example per term where the score reverses the pillar-local choice (e.g. accept a worse settlement to protect THE PEACE grade; decline a winnable coup because the target region cannot step up before the freeze). Without it the brief's requirement (e) 'what decision each score term changes' is unmet.

A comeback design for the player who is ECLIPSED/TRAILING at 1960 with no structural route back: new battlegrounds and FIRSTS are named, but nobody says what a trailing USA does in 1961 that a leading one cannot; without it 1960 is the quit checkpoint the genre analyst's abandonment-curve finding predicts.

The score for a war won by settlement: the ClientState clause paints the map, the SCARRED cap and casualty debit are the only brakes, and none of the six checks whether a limited conventional war in 1952 (no first use, under a million dead) is simply the best score play for the USSR. That is 'the big war win-able by accident' at one rung lower.

What minors can actually DO to their score in v1 (static SoL, zero slots, legitimacy only by scripted event): a list of minor-power verbs that move a term, or an explicit statement that minor scoring is read-only until those verbs exist.

A playtest falsification protocol beyond the hands-off harness: e.g. two testers play the same seed with and without the score visible; if their command logs do not diverge, the score has not changed a decision. The historian's 'if either superpower reads 1955 as a clear win the weights are wrong' is the only falsifiable statement in 90 pages; there should be one per term.

Cost of the reckoning page in reading time vs the 80-word card: verdict-legibility's caps (4 rows, 6 regions, 6 movers, 2 claim lines) and the historian's 6x2x3 table cannot both be the page; nobody reconciled the surface.

Save/replay and the 1970 end: does the campaign continue after the 1970 verdict (EU4 1821-style 'play on' with events through Sept 1970) and does a post-1970 exchange rewrite the verdict? Systems-integration hints at PLAY ON; the rule is unstated.
keep: Held-state scoring: freeze the trailing 12-month standing (or 'in band 6 of 12 months') and print 'HELD n OF 12' / 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD' on the mover line (genre-victory-systems, verdict-legibility, asymmetric-goals, board-game-scoring-cadence all converge; it is cheap, visible, and dull to game).

Catastrophe as a lexicographic gate above the score with attribution to the initiator and NO ranking printed on the funeral screen (board-game-scoring-cadence's three-state track and verdict-legibility's 'RUIN only, LEADING only in the past tense', minus the epitaph line).
A provocation ledger counting tension authored above the Crisis band, so making the AI fire first does not pay (genre-victory-systems, from Balance of Power 1990's Nastiness Index).

The monthly verdict sentence with a named cause and a panel key, changing only at month rollover, with a dead band and a two-month trend rule; no live number anywhere on the HUD (verdict-legibility 'THE STANDING LINE', war_ui ASSESSMENT template).

Own figures REPORTED for planners, rival figures as Kent-worded estimate brackets, truth printed beside belief only at the freeze (historian 'believed vs reckoned', systems-integration reuse of dashboard/observed_industry_centi).
Legitimacy as the single prestige currency that the score READS and never re-penalises, and the fact that it is spent at the settlement table (systems-integration).

One formula with column (West/East/DENIED) and reach regions as data, and a par_bid/difficulty that moves the baseline rather than the formula (board-game-scoring-cadence, asymmetric-goals, systems-integration).

Fixed, public checkpoint dates including 1970 as the close, keyed off influence.checkpoints.len(), with update_score as the first occupant of TickSet::Resolve and the three attribution counters added to existing resources (systems-integration).

The 1970 epilogue as prose from named voices with 'the three things that decided it', dated, and a DIVERGENCES column; no score-over-time chart, no 86-row ranking (genre-victory-systems, verdict-legibility, asymmetric-goals).
Publishing the scoring rule once, in words, in the founding edition (verdict-legibility).

The historian's calibration list (24 dated events with magnitudes) as a test oracle for the paper's headline weighting, and the hands-off assertion that neither superpower reads 1955 as a clear win or loss.

Score-aware AI at most in the self-grade form (the allocator reallocates toward its own worst region; pre-reckoning surge printed in the chequebook), never reading the player's ledger (asymmetric-goals, genre-victory-systems).

objections.target: verdict-legibility: THE HISTORICAL PAR (par.ron baked from the hands-off run); genre-victory-systems: THE RECKONING graded 'against the deterministic hands-off baseline'
objections.objection: The hands-off run is not a fixed table. Elections roll `swing = roll(-100..=100)` from `rng.fork(b"elections")` (influence.md Formulas) and coups roll from `rng.fork(b"coup")`, so the hands-off world at seed 1950 (the only seed the harnesses use: influence.rs:2976, events.rs:976) is one sample, not 'the record'. A par.ron generated at ship time is therefore wrong for every other seed, goes stale with every timeline corpus change (189 events landed in the last commit; the anchors test itself tolerates 3 mismatches in 40), and for a minor the 'baseline' is a nation nobody plays (the allocator runs only USA/SOV — influence.md AI allocator), i.e. par = 'do nothing'. Either the par is recomputed per seed at campaign start (a 15 s hidden run, and the AI's own reaction to the score, if adopted, makes it circular) or it is a script leak with a false claim of determinism. The 1950-tick-0 par (board-game-scoring-cadence) is seed-independent and is the only par that survives.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: THE LEDGER hands-off net '+2 West' from MAP -16 + OUTPUT +14 + STANDING +4
objections.objection: The 'narrow Western' hands-off verdict is manufactured by the two knobs the analyst admits are the only knobs (OUTPUT cap ±4, STANDING band values), chosen after seeing the MAP run. I reran `hands_off_bands` today and the map figures check out (1965: East Presence in AFRICA/ASIA/CENTRAL_AMERICA/MIDDLE_EAST, West Domination in EUROPE/SOUTH_AMERICA, Domination in CENTRAL_AMERICA after Cuba), but the map term is structurally biased the other way from what history says: every East asset is off the set (PRC is a seed row, influence.ron:142, not a battleground; Poland, GDR, the satellites likewise), so the Sino-Soviet split — hands-off PRC reads 'N +0' by 1965 — the largest correlation-of-forces shift of the window per the historian, scores ZERO, while Cuba scores as a full East gain. A verdict that reads 'East gaining' while the East is losing China is not history's verdict; it is a battleground-set artefact, and OUTPUT/STANDING are then tuned to cancel it. The harness assertion the analyst proposes will lock the artefact in.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: MOMENTUM term ('USSR ahead on momentum at 1955 and 1960, behind on both by 1970' as the calibration target)
objections.objection: No analyst checked whether the economy sim produces Soviet growth above American growth in 1950-63 and below after. planning.rs has one growth path for both systems (INVEST_CONVERT_PERMILLE 45, DEPRECIATION 2, planned default split 350/450/200 vs market invest 200-450 by interest rate) with no Kosygin-1965 slowdown, no extensive-growth exhaustion, and no 1963 harvest event feeding the industry index. If the hands-off USSR does not out-grow the hands-off USA in the sim (nobody printed `last_growth_centi` for the two poles), the MOMENTUM term tells the Soviet player 'BEHIND ON BOTH' from the first reckoning — exactly the failure the historian's own pitfall names — and the fix would be an economy retune disguised as a score design. The term is a claim about the economy that must be verified in the harness before it is a score line.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: 'Believed score versus reckoned score — the checkpoint freezes the truth and prints the gap'; verdict-legibility: THEIRS column 'estimate until the record is frozen, then as the record'
objections.objection: Printing the rival's true industry, arsenal and standings every five years on a calendar hands the US player Corona imagery for free and makes economic/nuclear penetration worthless in the year before a reckoning (intel.rs:170 `knowledge(viewer, subject, Domain)` exists precisely to narrow `observed_industry_centi`, planning.rs:131). Historically the missile gap closed through U-2 (1956), Corona (Aug 1960) and Gilpatric (Oct 1961) — intelligence and a political choice to publish — not a five-year almanac. It also contradicts systems-integration's correct reading of the epistemic contract (a score view is a viewer-parameterised function over an exact ledger). The rival's frozen card should stay an estimate through penetration forever; the 'YOU BELIEVED 3:1; IT WAS 6:1' reveal belongs to the 1970 retrospective only, when the campaign is over.

objections.target: genre-victory-systems: provocation ledger ('each tension write already has a named cause and an author')
objections.objection: False on the code: `GlobalTension::apply(&mut self, delta: i32)` (tension.rs:68) takes a bare delta; there is no author, no cause, no per-writer log. Events write tension via `AdjustTension(n)` with no country. Building the RESTRAINED/FORWARD/RECKLESS ledger requires threading an author through every tension write in events, crisis, nuclear, settlement and war-aims — a cross-cutting change to a determinism-critical resource — not 'a counter over existing tension events'. And timeline events (Berlin ultimatum, U-2, Tsar Bomba) apply tension with no player agency, so a hands-off superpower would be scored RECKLESS by the script.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: loss attribution ('WHO LOST X?' debits a domestic/credibility line at ~3x a gain)
objections.objection: On this sim the map moves mostly by timeline shove: Cuba 1959-61, Iraq 1958, Egypt 1955, Guinea 1958 are SetAlignment/ShiftAlignment events (world-timeline, events/09) that fire whether or not the player did anything. A 3x asymmetric debit on a scripted map means the hands-off USA is HUMILIATED on credibility by 1965 and the hands-off USSR is not (its losses — Ghana, Indonesia, Algeria — are mostly denied-column moves, not West gains, so they debit less under the same rule). Historically true that Eisenhower took the blame for Cuba; but the brief's test is that the hands-off world yields a contested verdict, and this term alone breaks it. If kept, it must be capped and only debit crossings the player could have contested (an open program slot existed), which is new state.

objections.target: genre-victory-systems: 'ECLIPSED on two terms fires a domestic pressure chain (Politburo/Cabinet/Junta variant chosen by the existing regime type)'
objections.objection: There is no regime type in the sim. The only 'regime' state is influence's `open: bool` (closed regimes halve PRESENCE, influence.rs:267) and `Military.stability`. No leader, cabinet, Politburo or succession model exists; the 1964 Khrushchev ouster is a timeline date. The write-back proposed is a new domestic-politics system with priced options for 86 nations, smuggled in as a score consequence. Either ship the score without it (the analyst's own pitfall says then 'ship nothing') or admit the dependency.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: CATASTROPHE TRACK — SCARRED if `crushed_count` rose to >= 2
objections.objection: Hands-off Moscow crushes Hungary (1956) and Czechoslovakia (1968) from the timeline, so the hands-off USSR is SCARRED and capped at COSTLY for the campaign without a player decision — and no contemporary put Prague 1968 in the same class as a million dead or a broken taboo; Moscow's price for it was legitimacy abroad (the Western CPs) and it is already paid that way via GrantLegitimacy events (SOV is the target of 11 grants). Crush itself costs nothing in legitimacy in code (influence.rs:505-520: lock, edge, crushed_count only), so the analyst is trying to price it in the score because the mechanic does not; that is the wrong layer. Drop the crush clause from SCARRED.

objections.target: ALL SIX (genre 'STANDING = legitimacy band'; historian 'never make prestige spendable'; board-game 'STANDING from legitimacy bands'; systems-integration 'prestige is the SAME number spent on settlement clauses')
objections.objection: Legitimacy IS a spent currency: settlement execution debits the proposer by the summed clause weight (settlement.rs:~1042, `legitimacy -= legit_cost`, gated at :745). The historian's pitfall ('every contemporary measure was a verdict derived from events, never a bank') is therefore violated by every analyst who reads `legitimacy_of` as the prestige/standing term: a player who buys a good peace at the table lowers their own score, and a player who hoards legitimacy for the reckoning refuses settlements — the opposite of the 'avoided catastrophe as shared positive' history the historian documents (Austria 1955, LTBT 1963 were prestige gains for both). Reading a bank balance as a verdict also fails the 'held state not event count' rule the genre analyst set. Something else has to be the prestige term, or legitimacy spent on treaties must be credited back.

objections.target: board-game-scoring-cadence: THE LEDGER STANDING term from legitimacy; the '+3 West on UNSC 83' first-hour beat
objections.objection: The legitimacy ledger is authored by the timeline and is structurally Western: 27 GrantLegitimacy event effects target USA against 11 for SOV in the events corpus, and the first one (UNSC 83, June 1950, +25) arrives before the player has done anything. A 'STANDING' term read straight from it is a scripted head start printed as the player's standing; the hands-off run would show the West 'leading on legitimacy alone' in month six, which is what the analyst's own first-hour test celebrates. Historically Korea's UN cover did help Washington — but a score term the timeline moves more than the player is a term with no verb, which breaks the house rule every analyst cites.

objections.target: asymmetric-goals-and-fun: 'BY THE LEDGER, [INITIATOR/AGAINST] WON. THE LEDGER IS ALL THAT SURVIVED.' on the funeral screen; cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: 'general exchange multiplies every other term by surviving population fraction'
objections.objection: Both print a winner under the mushroom cloud. Kahn's postwar-states table with a per-homeland survival multiplier literally ranks the two homelands by dead — that is DEFCON's Survivor mode in period dress, and it is the exact thing nuclear research principle 10 and endgame.rs:1-5/142 refuse. Systems-integration is right: `PoleCard` must have no field from which a post-exchange rank can be computed, and the only text is the LAST frozen era card in the past tense. 'X WON' will be the screenshot no matter how the sentence qualifies it.

objections.target: AI feedback: genre ('AI superpower reads its own grade and reallocates'), board-game ('ledger gap as risk appetite'; but also 'the AI must be checkpoint-blind'), asymmetric-goals ('pre-reckoning surge, marginal-region weight'), systems-integration ('keep the Ledger read-only for AI in v1')
objections.objection: Four incompatible answers, and the board-game analyst contradicts himself in one output. The coherence problem: if the AI reads the score, the hands-off baseline that two analysts want to grade against becomes a function of the AI's reaction to the score, and every scoring retune silently retunes the influence pillar's calibration harness (`hands_off_anchors_land_near_history`, influence.rs:2970). The risk-appetite mechanic additionally targets AI coups that do not exist ('once AI coups arrive in v1.5' — influence.md: AI never launches a coup in v1). Decide once: v1 AI is score-blind; the marginal-region multiplier is an allocator improvement to argue on its own merits in the influence doc, not here.

objections.target: Era aggregation: genre ('reset per era, median of four terms'), board-game ('sum of era deltas = board since 1950'), asymmetric-goals ('weights 1/2/3/4, end-weighted'), historian ('count of eras in which you led momentum')
objections.objection: Four different campaign-verdict aggregations with contradictory incentives: per-era reset says a 1955 collapse is forgiven; sum-of-deltas says it is permanent; 1:2:3:4 says 1970 is worth four 1955s and invites a fifteen-year turtle followed by a 1966-69 sprint — the exact snapshot-gaming the same analyst's 12-month ring is meant to stop. None cites a period source for its choice; history 'remembers how it ended' is an assertion. Pick the one with a mechanical justification (sum of deltas has the printable identity), and say what the others would do to the hands-off verdict.

objections.target: 'Held state' rings: genre (12-month standings ring, majority verdict), verdict-legibility ('in band 6 of last 12 months'), asymmetric-goals (trailing-12-month mean of every line)
objections.objection: Double-models hysteresis that already exists: band entry needs |pos| >= 300 evaluated at month rollover, reversal within 12 months runs at half rate, contested windows raise both thresholds to 300, a coup needs 90 days and one op slot (influence.md Formulas). The board-game analyst's flow-rate arithmetic (>= 3 months per flip at the theoretical maximum) is the honest bound. Adding a 6-of-12 rule on top means a legitimate, hysteresis-cleared November flip is 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD' — a second, invisible, slower hysteresis — while the existing paper line 'ON THE RECORD SINCE THE {year} RECKONING' (paper_ui.rs:596) and `Checkpoint { standings }` are a snapshot. A trailing mean of SoL/legitimacy is new ring state on three resources for a problem that only the map term has, and the map term is already protected.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: dated dimension unlocks (space 1957, growth race 1956-57, consumer standard 1959) and the FIRSTS register; asymmetric-goals: FIRSTS as Great Projects with era deadlines
objections.objection: Historically right that nobody scored space before Sputnik, but the mechanism as proposed is a script: 'sputnik' and 'gagarin-orbit' are Date-triggered timeline events (events/04:73,133), not projects anyone can win first. `GreatProjectDef.country` is a single sponsor ('only this country may build it', ugs-data lib.rs:521) and the only prestige payload is `Prestige { tension_relief }` — there is no race, no completion order, no 'first finisher' fact to read. A FIRSTS term therefore credits Moscow on 4 Oct 1957 by calendar in every campaign, which is a dimension that switches on with a scripted rival point and no player verb. Either the space race becomes a real multi-sponsor project race (a construction change) or FIRSTS is not a score term in v1.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: annual UNGA roll-call line ('THE MAJORITY HOLDS / SLIPS / IS GONE', the 1961 'important question' story)
objections.objection: The design doc already calls it tautological with alignment and the research deferred it; the analyst concedes the point and asks for it as a display unit. On this sim it is worse than tautological: there is no UN membership state, so the electorate is 'countries that exist', which counts Switzerland, both Germanys and the PRC seat wrongly (the PRC held no seat until Res. 2758, 1971 — Taipei voted), and the 1961 'important question' switch is a dated script leak. Fine as a paper flavour line derived from bands; it must not be a score input and must not be described as the 'public integer' of the score or the map term is counted twice.

objections.target: genre-victory-systems: 'ASCENDANT on ALIGNMENT grants one influence slot' (Splendour analogue)
objections.objection: A slot for leading is a snowball in the pillar the research spent most effort de-snowballing (influence.md killed fungible influence and per-country cash aid because they compounded). Rewarding the standings leader with more standings capacity is Vic2 prestige-compounding by another name and contradicts the analyst's own rule 3. If a write-back is required, it should flow to the trailer (the TS Space Race valve) or to no one.

objections.target: verdict-legibility: 'Frozen text stored with the checkpoint so a test can string-compare it across seeds'; systems-integration: sentences assembled in sim from `dashboard_industry_centi`
objections.objection: Boundary: rendered prose is presentation. `Influence::digest` deliberately excludes the wire and chequebook as narrative (influence.rs:288-298); storing English in the sim's frozen record and folding it into the digest means a copy edit desyncs saves. The ingredients (grade words, causes as ids, dates) belong in the frozen era card; the sentence belongs in ugs-app, exactly as `verdict_sentence` today is a pure function over state. Also 'byte-identical across seeds' is wrong — elections roll from the seed; identical across the two apps of the determinism test at the same seed is the claim.

objections.target: systems-integration: 'the score freeze must key off `influence.checkpoints.len()`' plus a 1970 close 'year == FINAL_YEAR && month == 1'
objections.objection: Internally inconsistent — it is two predicates after all — and `CHECKPOINT_YEARS = [1955,1960,1965]` (influence.rs:104) has no 1970 entry and no 1950 par entry; `new_month` is false at tick 0 so a tick-0 par cannot ride the same freeze. Cheap to fix (extend the array, seed the par in `seed` before the first command flush), but say so; as written the 1970 reckoning fires on a predicate the paper's 'ON THE RECORD SINCE' line does not know about.

objections.target: cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: bloc COHESION as a scored line (Suez, Hungary, Sino-Soviet, de Gaulle 1966, Prague)
objections.objection: Right dimension, no state. Cohesion of a bloc is not modelled: NATO/Cominform members are 600-month locks, the France-NATO exit event merely unlocks and shifts FRA -150 (events/03:276, FRA still reads 'W +700 NATO' in the hands-off 1965 board), the Sino-Soviet split moves a seed row that is not a battleground, and Suez has no alliance-strain effect. A cohesion line would be a scripted-event tally (crushed_count and OptionChosen ids) presented as a state, which the genre analyst's rule 'held state, not event count' forbids. Either add own-bloc lock-strength as a readable state or drop the line.

objections.target: asymmetric-goals-and-fun: sourced per-nation expectation rows (expectations.ron) for 86 nations
objections.objection: The row content proposed is half events ('Aswan financing', 'Belgrade 1961', 'East of Suez past January 1968', 'Decree 900 intact') despite the analyst's own pitfall that rows must be outcomes; and the outcome rows that remain (DENIED count in ASIA rising, 'field holds my region') are exogenous for a minor: in the hands-off run ASIA reads N5-6 and MIDDLE_EAST N4 because newborn states are born non-aligned by data, so a passive India 'meets' Panchsheel without a verb. 86 sourced rows × 4 checkpoints is also 344 hand-written historical judgments to maintain against a growing corpus, which is the second scoring system the brief forbids, relocated into data.

objections.target: systems-integration: 'nuclear Stage rank (Tested=+, Thermonuclear=+) in the prestige term'
objections.objection: UK 1952, France 1960, PRC 1964 arrive from data (nuclear.rs:78-89) — a prestige credit for a scripted test date is a term the player does not own, and for the two superpowers the counting is done by 1953. It adds nothing after 1955 except a permanent +n for having a bomb, i.e. exactly the compounding the genre analyst warned about. Deterrence already keys off the rival's estimate of the arsenal (nuclear research principle 4); prestige from tests is double-modelling.

missing: A hands-off harness print of the proposed verdict for BOTH poles at 1955/1960/1965/1970 before any weight is chosen — no analyst ran the economy or legitimacy side; only the map was run (I reran `hands_off_bands`: the map numbers quoted by board-game-scoring-cadence are correct, everything else is asserted).

An answer for the Sino-Soviet split and every other locked-then-unlocked bloc asset: the battleground set excludes the East's 1950 holdings, so the map term cannot see the East losing China (hands-off PRC 'N +0' by 1965) or the West losing France; every analyst's 'alignment' term inherits this blind spot.

Tension authorship: `GlobalTension::apply(delta)` has no author (tension.rs:68), so provocation ledgers, credibility debits and 'rungs you climbed' are all uncomputable until every tension write carries a country — a determinism-critical cross-cutting change that must be designed, not assumed.

Attribution for the taboo: `taboo_broken: bool` (nuclear.rs:226) records no user or tick; systems-integration is the only analyst who noticed that every 'ceiling keyed on the attributed user' depends on a field that does not exist.

What legitimacy is: a spent settlement currency (settlement.rs:745, ~1042) authored mostly by timeline grants (27 USA-targeted effects vs 11 SOV). No analyst reconciled 'prestige = legitimacy band' with 'prestige must not be a bank' or with the fact that the script writes it.

A rule for scripted map moves versus player-caused ones: the timeline's SetAlignment/ShiftAlignment shoves (Cuba, Iraq, Egypt, Guinea) drive most band crossings in the hands-off run; loss-attribution and credibility debits need to know whether the player could have contested the crossing (an open slot, an unlocked target), which is state nobody proposed.

Seed dependence of any 'historical par': elections and coups roll from the seed, so a shipped par.ron is a one-seed sample; the alternative (tick-0 par) is seed-free but blind to everything the timeline does.

The endgame's date arithmetic (`tick / (24*365)`, endgame.rs:49-50) drifts across the 1952/56/60/64/68 leap years — a cheap bug every verdict screen will inherit; only systems-integration caught it and nobody proposes the GameDate fix as a prerequisite.

The 1965-70 span: `CHECKPOINT_YEARS` has no 1970 entry and the corpus ends 1970-09-04 (Vietnam escalation, Prague, Apollo all fall in the last era); several analysts treat 1970 as 'the close' with no proposal for what a player does between the 1970 reckoning and the end date, and `the_world_turns_to_1970` asserts only that 1970 is not a world war.
keep: board-game-scoring-cadence: score the map as DELTA from a tick-0 1950 par (Twilight Struggle's zero marker), never absolutely — the structurally Western battleground set makes any absolute reading a permanent blowout (I confirmed the 1965 hands-off board), and the tick-0 par is seed-independent, deterministic and cheap.

board-game-scoring-cadence + systems-integration + asymmetric-goals: catastrophe is a lexicographic state above the score (UNSCARRED / SCARRED / RUINED or a verdict ceiling), never a subtraction; general exchange prints no rank and no winner anywhere; `PoleCard` keeps no field a post-exchange rank could be computed from; the funeral gains at most one past-tense line from the last frozen era card. This is exactly nuclear research principle 10 and endgame.rs:142.

systems-integration: the score is a pure monthly fold over existing digest-stable resources in the empty `TickSet::Resolve` (lib.rs:63, no systems registered — confirmed), freezing on the existing checkpoint predicate; the three attribution fields (`first_use` user+tick, crisis prevailed/stood_down, `Treaty.proposer` — confirmed missing at settlement.rs:236) are added beside their mechanics and folded into those digests; register in SimPlugin, `reset_sim`, tests/determinism.rs and the savegame digest. The `LivingStandards` observation is stale in one respect — it is written monthly at planning.rs:437 and agriculture.rs:215 despite the 'Static in v1' doc comment — so the SoL term is live but still needs a digest.

Epistemic contract for the rival's column: own figures via `dashboard_industry_centi` (reported for planned), rival via `observed_industry_centi(t, intel.knowledge(me, t, Economic))`, legitimacy public, casualties exact for self and ranged for others; Kent words and bands only; estimate-width fallback to EVEN (verdict-legibility, systems-integration) — provided the frozen card stays an estimate and never reveals truth on the calendar.

One column choice, not one formula per nation: `alignment_of` and `RegionStanding { west, east, denied }` already give every nation its column; the denied column scored through the same `verdict()` (board-game, systems-integration) is the right shape for India/Egypt/Yugoslavia, with the caveat that for minors the field's count is mostly exogenous and needs a verb attached.

verdict-legibility: no HUD number, verdict words that can change only at month rollover with a dead band and a two-consecutive-months arrow rule; one verdict sentence per term naming region/figure/event and the panel key (the war_ui.rs ASSESSMENT template); the epilogue as three dated causes, not a twelve-line breakdown; publish the rule once in words in the founding edition.

cold-war-scorekeeping-historian: the calibration list of 24 dated score events with magnitudes is the best-sourced artefact in the set and should become the harness's anchor table for the verdict (which reckoning should read what, for whom), independent of which mechanism is chosen; the distinction between momentum and level is historically right and must be verified against the economy sim before it becomes a term.

genre-victory-systems: the negative catalogue — reject DEFCON scoring, reject cumulative Fame/Vic2 prestige compounding, reject checklists (Vic3 objectives, Civ VII legacy paths), reject a superpower-only board — and the observation that the checkpoint must feed something back or be inert; the specific write-backs proposed do not survive, the requirement does.

asymmetric-goals: the turtle objection (an avoided-catastrophe line with no demand for movement makes 'sit on 1950' the dominant USA play) and the 'ceiling not subtraction' argument for limited use; and the warning that a taboo ceiling must key on the attributed user, never the global flag.

principles.principle: Score the map as a signed DELTA from a tick-0 1950 par through the existing three-column regional verdict (West/East/Denied via `verdict()` and Twilight Struggle region values); never absolutely, and never against a hands-off 'historical par'.
principles.support: board-game-scoring-cadence (ran `hands_off_bands`: absolute TS values give West +41 in 1950 and +28 in 1965, a blowout; as deltas the same run reads East +13 by 1965), systems-integration (`RegionStanding { west, east, denied }` and `alignment_of` already give every nation its column), asymmetric-goals (column + reach as data). Both skeptics KEEP the tick-0 par explicitly and KILL par.ron: elections and coups roll from the seed so a shipped par is a one-seed sample, it goes stale with every timeline commit, and it grades a passive USA 'AS HISTORY'. Precedent: TS's marker starts at zero on the opening placement; tournament imbalance is fixed by bidding the par, not the table.

principles.principle: Four fixed, public freezes (1955, 1960, 1965, 1970 as the close) and the campaign score is the SUM of era deltas, so 'sum of the eras = the board since 1950' is a printable identity. No per-era reset, no end-weighting, no auto-win.
principles.support: board-game-scoring-cadence (snapshot deltas, identity), systems-integration (freeze keyed off the existing checkpoint predicate, extend `CHECKPOINT_YEARS`), verdict-legibility and genre (the Reckoning as the scoring-card moment; Civ VI R&F and Pax Pamir on periodic reckonings as stopping/resumption points). history-skeptic asked for one aggregation with a mechanical justification: reset-per-era yields a static median grade (fun-skeptic, serious), 1:2:3:4 weighting invites a fifteen-year turtle then a sprint (history-skeptic); sum-of-deltas is the only one with a printable identity and banked history (Cuba after 1960 does not erase 1960).

principles.principle: Catastrophe is a lexicographic state ABOVE the score (UNSCARRED / SCARRED / EXCHANGE). The funeral screen prints the dead, the initiator, and how long the peace held, and NOTHING that orders the poles in any tense; a SCARRED ceiling always has a slope beneath it.
principles.support: systems-integration (`PoleCard` must hold no field from which a post-exchange rank can be computed; Crawford's rule already at endgame.rs:1-5/142; TS DEFCON-1 'phasing player loses'), verdict-legibility ('RUIN only'), board-game (three-state track). fun-skeptic FATAL objection resolved: the survival multiplier (historian), the epitaph ledger line (board-game), 'BY THE LEDGER X WON' (asymmetric-goals) and even systems-integration's past-tense 'THE LAST RECKONING HAD READ' are all cut — the last is a ranking in the past tense and would be the screenshot. fun-skeptic serious objection on ceilings ('a zero with a delay and a free second shot') resolved by the PEACE slope: every attributed use and every 2-per-10,000 of own dead keeps debiting inside the COSTLY class. history-skeptic: `crushed_count` removed from SCARRED (hands-off Moscow crushes Hungary and Prague by timeline; crush is priced in legitimacy grants, wrong layer).

principles.principle: Words, not numbers: one monthly verdict sentence with a named cause and a panel key, changing only at month rollover, with a dead band and a two-consecutive-months arrow rule; no live figure on the HUD; the rule is published once in prose in the founding edition.
principles.support: verdict-legibility (Civ VI World Rankings vs its ignored Score tab; Vic2's decomposed rank vs Vic3's decimal prestige; the war_ui.rs ASSESSMENT template as the house pattern), genre (five words, not six-digit Fame), systems-integration (`verdict_sentence`/`kent_word` already exist), asymmetric-goals, historian. Both skeptics KEEP. Vocabulary fixed here so six lexicons collapse to three: monthly GAINING / HOLDING / SLIPPING (bloc leaders add LEADING / EVEN / TRAILING head-to-head); era STALEMATE / NARROW / CLEAR / DECISIVE with GAIN or LOSS; campaign WON / HELD / LOST, COSTLY as the SCARRED ceiling class, EXCHANGE unranked.

principles.principle: Epistemic contract: own figures via `dashboard_industry_centi` (REPORTED for planners), the rival's via `observed_industry_centi` through economic penetration as a two-significant-figure Kent-worded bracket; a verdict word the bracket cannot decide falls back to EVEN; the frozen card stays an estimate; belief and truth sit side by side only in the 1970 final edition.
principles.support: systems-integration (machinery exists: planning.rs:116-139, intel.rs:170, paper_ui.rs est_men_range), verdict-legibility (OURS / THEIR ESTIMATE / AS THEY CLAIM; Kent 1964), historian (the 1957-62 double belief; missile gap; Riazan), asymmetric-goals (the fogged score). history-skeptic's serious objection — un-fogging the rival every five years on the calendar hands over Corona imagery for free and makes penetration worthless before a reckoning — is accepted: the reveal moves to 1970 only. fun-skeptic's note that fog is texture, not the anti-coasting mechanism, is accepted; coasting is handled by the tick-0 par and the score-blind AI allocator pushing the map (see shape).

principles.principle: One formula for 86 nations; all asymmetry lives in three data fields per playable nation — column (from the live band; DENIED for non-aligned), reach regions, and scale (1 superpower, 2 middle, 3 minor) — with a documented default (own region, scale 3). No expectation rows, no per-archetype rulesets.
principles.support: board-game (Labyrinth: asymmetric targets on one board; QMG: Cold War's bespoke third-faction victory as the counterexample), systems-integration, asymmetric-goals (the Football Manager expectation idea survives only as flavour), historian (Nasser lost the war and won the era on the same six dimensions read from his own 1950 line). history-skeptic's objection to 344 hand-written expectation rows (a second scoring system relocated into data) and fun-skeptic's objection that archetype rows would be the real system are both accepted: rows are cut. fun-skeptic's minor-power objection is accepted honestly rather than papered over: in v1 a zero-slot minor's MAP line is read-only and the paper says so ('NO STANDING PROGRAMS: MINOR POWER — YOUR LEDGER MOVES ON OUTPUT AND STANDING'); scale 3 makes those two terms decisive for it.

principles.principle: The score is a pure monthly fold over existing digest-stable resources, the first occupant of the empty `TickSet::Resolve`; the only new sim facts are three attribution counters added beside the mechanics that produce them (`first_use` user+tick, crisis prevailed/stood_down, `Treaty.proposer`); rendered prose lives in ugs-app, never in the digest.
principles.support: systems-integration (decisive, code-cited: lib.rs:63 Resolve has zero systems; nuclear.rs:226/580 records no user; settlement.rs:236 drops the proposer; four registries to touch). history-skeptic KEEPS and adds the corrections adopted here: freeze on one predicate (extend `CHECKPOINT_YEARS` to include 1970, seed the 1950 par in `seed` before the first command flush since `new_month` is false at tick 0), sim stores ids/ints and the app renders sentences (verdict-legibility's frozen-prose test is rewritten as 'byte-identical rendered text across the two apps of the determinism test at the same seed'), fix endgame.rs:49-50 to use `GameDate` for leap years, give `LivingStandards` a digest and export `population_by_holder`.

principles.principle: The AI is score-blind in v1 and the checkpoint writes nothing back into the sim that compounds; the score's one bite on play is that legitimacy is both the STANDING term and the currency spent at the settlement table.
principles.support: systems-integration ('keep the Ledger read-only for AI in v1'), asymmetric-goals ('score-aware, never score-chasing'), both skeptics (four incompatible AI answers; a score-reading AI makes the influence calibration harness a function of score tuning; the risk-appetite loop is a reverse thermostat that rewards sandbagging and DEFCON-suicide from the leader's side — killed). genre's 'checkpoint must feed something back' requirement stands but its proposed write-backs (slot for ASCENDANT, Politburo chain, legitimacy debit) are killed as Vic2/EU4 compounding and as depending on a regime model that does not exist (history-skeptic). fun-skeptic's 'only real cost in ninety pages' — spending standing to buy peace terms — becomes the centrepiece: settlement clauses debit legitimacy (settlement.rs:1033-1044) and the PEACE term credits the settlement, so the trade is explicit and printed.

principles.principle: Legitimacy is READ by the score, never re-penalised, and every act the score would otherwise punish twice (coups, exposed ops, exploitation zones, crush) is priced where it happens; treaty-spending of legitimacy is credited on the PEACE side so a good peace is never a score loss.
principles.support: systems-integration (double-charging pitfall: settlement.rs:1375, influence.rs:87-93 already move legitimacy), historian (Austria 1955, hotline/LTBT 1963, NPT 1968 were scored as prestige gains for both parties). history-skeptic's serious objection that legitimacy is a spent bank (settlement.rs:1033-1044) and structurally scripted (27 USA-targeted grants vs 11 SOV) is answered two ways: STANDING is a small delta term (one point per 25 legitimacy, cap 3 per era) so the scripted head start is worth at most NARROW, and the PEACE credit for executed war treaties (+2 each) refunds the spend in the term where contemporaries booked it.

principles.principle: The verdict is prose from named voices — one sentence per byline, THE THREE THINGS THAT DECIDED IT as dated lines pointing at a frozen row or a fired event, and the four era cards as words — never an 86-row ranking, a score-over-time chart, or a twelve-line breakdown.
principles.support: verdict-legibility (Suzerain slides, Frostpunk's one sentence, CK3 Legacy as the counterexample), genre (Hidden Agenda's biased press verdicts; the final edition with three bylines), asymmetric-goals (no moralising rider; DIVERGENCES as the replay hook, deferred), historian (verdict as biased press). Both skeptics KEEP. Frostpunk's 'But was it worth it?' is excluded: COSTLY is a fact about the ledger, printed with the bill, not an editorial.

synthesis.shape:
STATE. One resource `Ledger` in ugs-sim (new `score.rs`): `par: Board` frozen in `seed` at tick 0; `eras: Vec<EraCard>` pushed at the 1955/1960/1965/1970 freezes on the existing checkpoint predicate (extend `tuning::CHECKPOINT_YEARS` to four entries); `end: Option<CampaignEnd>` = `Reckoning(1970)` or `Exchange { initiator, tick }`. An `EraCard` holds, per playable nation, four signed integers (MAP, OUTPUT, STANDING, PEACE), the era's catastrophe state, the cause ids behind each term (region ids, battleground tags, event ids, dates — never strings), plus the exact inputs needed for the 1970 reveal (own actual industry per capita, own reported, legitimacy, dead). The three attribution fields go beside their mechanics: `NuclearPrograms.first_use: Option<(CountryTag, u64)>`, `Crises.prevailed/stood_down: BTreeMap<CountryTag,u16>`, `Treaty.proposer`. Registered in SimPlugin, `reset_sim`, tests/determinism.rs and the savegame digest in the same PR; `LivingStandards` gains a digest; `population_by_holder` is exported. No f64; years from `GameDate`.

CADENCE. `update_score` is the first system in `TickSet::Resolve` (after Politics, so it sees this month's standings and month-end production), body gated on `clock.new_month`; monthly it recomputes a provisional era card (MAP/OUTPUT/STANDING/PEACE since the last freeze) for the paper and freezes it when `influence.checkpoints.len() > ledger.eras.len()`. It also runs the tick a `GameOver` resource appears, sets `end = Exchange`, and stops updating cards. The AI allocator never reads it.

SURFACES (three, no panel, no HUD number). (1) THE STANDING: a monthly line in the paper's WORLD IN NUMBERS rail — 'OUR STANDING: SLIPPING — ASIA RUNS AGAINST US [P] — NEXT RECKONING JAN 1955 (54 MONTHS)'. Word from the provisional era score with a dead band of ±1 (scaled); cause = the term with the largest contribution in the verdict's direction, templated to a region/figure/event (the war_ui ASSESSMENT pattern); pointer = the panel key that owns the term (MAP→[P] politics, OUTPUT→[E] economy, STANDING→treaty table, PEACE→atomic/crisis dossier). Bloc leaders get a second line 'HEAD TO HEAD: PROBABLY LEADING MOSCOW (EST.)' with the Kent qualifier; if the rival's estimate bracket is wider than the margin the word is EVEN. An arrow appears only after two consecutive months in the same direction. A one-word HUD chip mirrors the word and opens the paper at the rail. The founding edition carries HOW THE CENTURY IS SCORED in period prose (four terms, four dates, non-aligned counts against both, catastrophes are never forgiven, an exchange ends the record) and the six regional verdict words for both poles — no numbers. (2) THE RECKONING: a special edition at each freeze, pauses once with [SPACE: PLAY ON] [N: FOLD]. Fixed layout under an 80-word cap for the summary card: computed banner from a six-template set; WHERE WE STAND — four rows × OURS (exact word; planners' own OUTPUT through the bureau's reported figure) / THEIRS (bracket, AS-OF stamp, '?' and 'MOSCOW DOES NOT PUBLISH' below LIMITED coverage) / VERDICT; THE MAP BY REGION — six regional verdict words with counts, the narrowest margin marked THE PRIZE; MOVERS — up to six battlegrounds with 'BAND SINCE DATE — CAUSE' from the wire ring; AS THEY SEE IT — two lines rendered from the rival's REPORTED figures in their masthead voice; the era grade word with sign ('NARROW GAIN') and the identity line 'THE ERAS SO FAR SUM TO THE BOARD SINCE 1950: EAST +6'. Every later monthly paper prints 'ON THE RECORD SINCE THE {year} RECKONING' beneath the live line. Rival columns remain estimates at every freeze. (3) THE FINAL EDITION at 1970-01-01: masthead class word (WON / HELD / LOST / COSTLY), one verdict sentence per byline (own organ, rival organ, the non-aligned Gazette), THE THREE THINGS THAT DECIDED IT (the three (term, era-or-event) contributions of largest absolute value, ties by date then tag, each a dated templated line), the four era cards as a 4×4 grid of words, and — only here — BELIEF BESIDE THE RECORD for both the rival's columns and the planner's own reported-vs-actual output.

THE VERDICT RULE. Era score S = MAP + OUTPUT + STANDING + PEACE (formula field). Era grade from |S × scale|: 0-1 STALEMATE, 2-5 NARROW, 6-11 CLEAR, 12+ DECISIVE, with GAIN or LOSS from the sign. Campaign C = S1955 + S1960 + S1965 + S1970; class from C × scale: ≥ +8 WON, −7..+7 HELD, ≤ −8 LOST. Head-to-head for the two poles = sign of S(USA) − S(SOV) with dead band 2. Catastrophe gate, worst era wins: UNSCARRED → class by C; SCARRED (an attributed nuclear use by you this era, or own dead in the era ≥ 30 per 10,000 of own 1950 population) → class capped at COSTLY, printed with the bill ('COSTLY — THE LEDGER READ CLEAR GAIN, AT A PRICE: THE TABOO BROKEN AT THE YALU, 1951; 1.2M DEAD'), the slope continuing inside the class through PEACE; EXCHANGE → no class for any nation on earth. A SCARRED era prints a black rule and the word in the masthead strip at the time, so the cap is never a 1970 surprise.

CAMPAIGN END. The 1970-01-01 freeze sets `end = Reckoning(1970)`, opens the final edition, pauses once; PLAY ON continues through the corpus (events to 1970-09-04) and beyond with no further reckonings and no ledger updates — except the catastrophe gate: a post-1970 general exchange still replaces the verdict with the funeral and stores EXCHANGE. On `GameOver` at any date the existing funeral screen is kept verbatim (cities, exact dead, initiator, 'THE PEACE HELD N YEARS' fixed to GameDate, 'WE DO NOT REWARD FAILURE') and gains exactly one line: the date of the last paper. No ledger, no epitaph, no past-tense standing, no Kahn table. Limited use by the AI never caps the player: SCARRED keys on `first_use.0 == player` (and later attributed uses), never on the global `taboo_broken`.

ASYMMETRY. Three data fields per playable nation in `assets/data/scenario/1950/scorecards.ron` (validated at load, default = own region, scale 3): USA/SOV reach = all six regions, scale 1; GBR EUROPE+MIDDLE_EAST+ASIA+AFRICA scale 2; FRA EUROPE+AFRICA+MIDDLE_EAST scale 2; PRC/IND ASIA scale 2; EGY MIDDLE_EAST+AFRICA scale 2; YUG EUROPE scale 2. Column is the nation's live alignment band at each freeze (DENIED for NonAligned; a France that leaves NATO still scores West until its band changes; a PRC that leaves the lock and reads N scores the field). MAP deltas are computed in the nation's current column at both ends. The rival for OUTPUT is the other pole's leader for a bloc member and the world median for the field. Difficulty and multiplayer move the par (`par_bid`, deferred), never the formula.

WHAT IT FEEDS. In v1 the score feeds the paper (three surfaces), the endgame, and one decision cost: legitimacy is the STANDING term and the settlement currency, so every clause bought at the table is a visible score trade whose peace is credited back under PEACE. The hands-off harness gains `hands_off_verdict` printing all four era cards for both poles and asserting the tuning targets. Nothing else in the sim reads the Ledger.

tensions.tension: Era aggregation: per-era reset with a median grade (genre), sum of era deltas (board-game), end-weighted 1:2:3:4 (asymmetric-goals), count of eras led on momentum (historian).
tensions.recommendation: Sum of era deltas. Reset produces a grade that cannot move (fun-skeptic: median{ALIGNMENT, SYSTEMS, HOLDING, HOLDING} = HOLDING for both poles in 1960); end-weighting invites a fifteen-year turtle then a 1966-69 sprint; momentum-era counting is one term, not an aggregation. The sum has the printable identity 'sum of the eras = the board since 1950', banks history (a 1955 collapse is permanent, as it was), and shows each era's own sign so a held lead reads STALEMATE for the era and WON for the campaign — which answers the 'reset resentment' worry without a reset.

tensions.tension: Does the AI read the score? Read-only (systems-integration), self-grade reallocation (genre), pre-reckoning surge and marginal-region weight (asymmetric-goals), ledger gap as risk appetite (board-game, who also says the AI must be checkpoint-blind).
tensions.recommendation: Score-blind in v1, full stop. The risk-appetite loop is a reverse thermostat (a lead makes the AI reckless, so the leader sandbags or baits a first strike — the DEFCON-suicide play from the leader's side) and targets AI coups that do not exist. A score-reading AI also makes `hands_off_anchors_land_near_history` a function of score tuning. The marginal-region multiplier and pre-reckoning surge are allocator improvements to argue in docs/design/systems/influence.md on their own merits; if adopted there, the paper prints 'MOSCOW PLAYS THE CALENDAR' in the chequebook line.

tensions.tension: Checkpoint write-backs: 'ship the write-backs (slot, Politburo chain, legitimacy debit) or ship nothing' (genre) versus 'no write-back that compounds' (fun-skeptic) and 'no regime model exists' (history-skeptic).
tensions.recommendation: Ship no write-backs in v1; the score is a reckoning surface plus one cost (legitimacy spent at the settlement table, credited under PEACE). Rewarding the leader with a slot is Vic2 prestige compounding inside the pillar the influence research spent most effort de-snowballing; the domestic chain needs a domestic-politics system the sim does not have. When a regime model arrives, write-backs must be counter-cyclical only (the TRAILING pole's domestic 'do something' mandate unlocks a verb; the leader gets scrutiny), never a capacity grant to the leader.

tensions.tension: The comparator: a hands-off historical par baked at ship time (genre, verdict-legibility), sourced expectation rows per nation (asymmetric-goals), or the tick-0 par plus the rival (board-game, systems-integration).
tensions.recommendation: Tick-0 par for MAP and STANDING, own previous-freeze figure for OUTPUT growth, the rival pole (or world median) as the head-to-head comparator. The hands-off world is seed-dependent (elections and coups roll), stale on every corpus commit, invisible to the player, and grades passivity as 'AS HISTORY'; expectation rows are 344 historical judgments that would be the second scoring system relocated into data. The hands-off run keeps exactly one job: a harness sanity band (see formula), never a displayed target. Sourced 'THE RECORD SAYS' flavour lines for the founding edition are welcome as non-scoring prose, deferred.

tensions.tension: OUTPUT as level (board-game: clamp of per-capita difference, +3/+4 West every era) versus momentum (historian: the USSR led on rate 1955-60 and lost on both by 1970), with the history-skeptic noting nobody verified the economy sim produces Soviet out-growth in the 1950s.
tensions.recommendation: Score growth since the previous freeze against the rival's growth (momentum), never level: level is a constant the Soviet player cannot move and a third of the score would be a spreadsheet line. Momentum is movable by investment share (`set_planned_allocation`, market interest rate) and is the historically documented term. Gate: the term ships only after `hands_off_verdict` prints both poles' five-year growth; if the planned system does not out-grow the market in 1950-60 that is an economy calibration item (no Kosygin slowdown, no extensive-growth exhaustion in planning.rs) to be fixed in the economy doc, not by re-weighting the score. Level prints in the paper as context ('OUTPUT AHEAD BY HALF, SOVIET FIGURES ESTIMATED') and is not scored.

tensions.tension: Legitimacy as the prestige/STANDING term (all six analysts) versus 'legitimacy is a spent settlement currency authored mostly by the timeline' (history-skeptic) and 'prestige must never be a bank' (historian).
tensions.recommendation: Keep legitimacy as the only world-opinion currency and read it — but as a small delta term (one point per 25, cap 3 per era) so the scripted UNSC 83 grant is worth +1, not a lead; and credit executed war treaties under PEACE (+2 each, cap +4 per era) so the player who spends 25 legitimacy on a good peace nets roughly zero on STANDING and positive on PEACE, matching how contemporaries booked Austria 1955 and the LTBT. Hoarding for the freeze is capped at +3 and costs the wars it could have ended. Crush should cost legitimacy in the influence mechanic (it costs nothing at influence.rs:505-520 today) — an influence-doc fix, not a score clause.

tensions.tension: Held-state scoring: a 12-month ring and 6-of-12 rule (genre, verdict-legibility, asymmetric-goals) versus 'the influence hysteresis already bounds the flip rate and a second invisible hysteresis is worse' (history-skeptic); the fun-skeptic keeps the ring.
tensions.recommendation: No new ring state in v1. The map cannot be sprinted: a band crossing needs |pos| ≥ 300 evaluated at rollover (≥ 3 months at the theoretical maximum flow, ~30 at usual rates), reversal runs at half rate for 12 months, one op slot with 90-day prep caps coups at one per quarter, and elections fall on sourced dates. OUTPUT is a five-year growth delta by construction; STANDING is capped small. The visible fix is the MOVERS list with 'BAND SINCE DATE' so a December coup is seen for what it is — a bounded, priced TS scoring-card play — rather than silently discounted. Revisit rings only if playtest logs show Q4 aid dumps exceeding the eighteen-month campaign the flow rates predict.

tensions.tension: Limited nuclear use: subtraction (genre: cap at ECLIPSED), verdict ceiling with no slope (asymmetric-goals), or 'a ceiling is a zero with a delay and a free second shot' (fun-skeptic).
tensions.recommendation: Ceiling with a slope. SCARRED caps the campaign class at COSTLY (so the province a battlefield weapon wins can never buy a WON verdict — no computable trade), and PEACE keeps debiting −4 per attributed use and −1 per 2/10,000 of own 1950 population dead beneath the cap, so the second and tenth use still cost and the era cards keep moving for the rest of the campaign. Deterrence itself stays in the crisis and nuclear systems (patron ultimatum, dropped AI thresholds, collapsing neutral alignment); the score only refuses the reward. No hall-of-records ordering of catastrophes: EXCHANGE is a single unranked class.

tensions.tension: When the truth is revealed: the frozen checkpoint prints belief beside truth (historian, verdict-legibility) versus the rival's card stays an estimate forever except in the 1970 retrospective (history-skeptic, systems-integration).
tensions.recommendation: Truth only in the 1970 final edition.
