A five-year calendar reveal makes economic and nuclear penetration worthless in the year before a reckoning and hands the US player Corona for free; historically the gap closed through U-2, Corona and a political choice to publish (Gilpatric, October 1961). The sim stores the exact inputs in the frozen card (deterministic, needed for the reveal); every rendering before 1970 goes through the viewer's penetration, including the planner's own reported OUTPUT. 'YOU BELIEVED 3:1 AGAINST; IT WAS 6:1 FOR' becomes the best line of the final edition.

tensions.tension: How many terms: six dated lines with MOMENTUM and STANDING words (historian) versus four (genre, board-game three, verdict-legibility four, systems-integration four).
tensions.recommendation: Four: MAP, OUTPUT, STANDING, PEACE. Cohesion has no state (locks are 600-month constants, Suez has no alliance strain), credibility double-counts legitimacy, strategic balance is deterrence's number and already keys the rival's arsenal estimate, nuclear-stage prestige credits scripted test dates, FIRSTS credit a Date-triggered Sputnik with no race to win, and the UNGA roll-call is the map counted twice with no UN membership state. All of these stay as newspaper flavour and calibration oracles (the historian's 24-event list becomes the headline-weighting test table), none as score inputs.

tensions.tension: Casualty thresholds: an absolute 1,000,000 dead SCARRED line (board-game) versus per-capita (fun-skeptic: one formula for 86 nations cannot use a headcount that is 0.6% of the USA and three Luxembourgs).
tensions.recommendation: Per-capita on own 1950 population everywhere: PEACE debits 1 per 2/10,000 dead (Korea reads −1 for the USA, −3 for the PRC), SCARRED at 30/10,000 in one era (USA ~460k, USSR ~540k, PRC ~1.65M), and a scripted Korean War never scars the PRC. The exact dead print only on the war report and the funeral; the score prints the band word.

tensions.tension: Minor powers: 'one formula already serves them' (board-game: Japan wins on OUTPUT) versus 'the minor's game is two terms they cannot move — a first-hour quit point for 60 of 86 nations' (fun-skeptic).
tensions.recommendation: Be honest in the doc and the paper: for a zero-slot minor the MAP line is read-only in v1 and the paper says so with the term it CAN move ('YOUR LEDGER MOVES ON OUTPUT AND STANDING'); scale 3 makes those decisive (a +2 OUTPUT era is CLEAR GAIN for Luxembourg). `LivingStandards` is in fact written monthly (history-skeptic corrected the 'static' doc comment) so the economy panel's investment verbs move OUTPUT, and treaties move STANDING/PEACE. A denial/alignment-declaration verb for minors is the first post-v1 item so the field's column stops being exogenous.

tensions.tension: The Sino-Soviet blind spot: every East 1950 holding (PRC, Poland, GDR, the satellites) is a locked seed row off the battleground set, so the map term cannot see the East losing China or the West losing France (history-skeptic, unanswered by any analyst).
tensions.recommendation: Accept and state the limit in v1: MAP measures the contested world, which is what both sides' Third World counts measured; the hands-off 'East gaining' reading is the CIA's 1958 aid-table reading, not a bug. The paper prints the split as the wire headline it already is. A COHESION term returns only when lock strength is readable state (a great-power defection from a bloc could then score as a MAP event in the defector's region at value DOMINATION); do not tune OUTPUT/STANDING to cancel the artefact, and do not lock the artefact into a numeric harness target — the harness asserts bands, not integers.

tensions.tension: Loss attribution ('WHO LOST X?' debiting at 3× a gain — historian) versus 'on this sim the map moves mostly by timeline shove and the hands-off USA would be HUMILIATED by script' (history-skeptic) and 'a 3× debit says never let a client wobble' (fun-skeptic).
tensions.recommendation: Cut from the score in v1; keep the headline. The MAP delta already scores a lost battleground symmetrically and the paper leads with 'WHO LOST CUBA?' in the player's own organ as flavour. A capped credibility debit returns only with contestability state (was an unlocked slot available when the crossing happened), which nobody has designed, and only after the war system can produce the Vietnam that the cap is meant to make cheaper than the escalation.

tensions.tension: The turtle: an avoided-catastrophe score lets the USA sit on 1950 (asymmetric-goals) — solved there by expectation rows that demand movement, which the skeptics killed as a checklist.
tensions.recommendation: The tick-0 par plus a score-blind AI allocator solve it without rows: hands-off, Moscow's allocator pushes the contested map East (0 / −6 / −7 for the West by 1965 on the numbers actually run) and the planned economy out-grows the market in the 1950s if the economy is calibrated, so a passive USA reads SLIPPING by 1957 and LOST on MAP by 1965; passivity is not 'AS HISTORY', it is losing ground. The USSR cannot turtle either: OUTPUT is momentum versus the rival and the 1960s slowdown arrives. PEACE credits require ending wars, not avoiding them, and Brink months cost both poles; no term rewards inaction.

synthesis.first_hour_acid_test:
Setup: paused at 1950-01-01, open the paper with N, play to July 1950, then run the hands-off harness to the 1955 freeze. Pass/fail is whether a tester who has opened only the paper can say, in one sentence, which term is dragging their standing and which key acts on it — and whether nothing numeric about score appears anywhere.

AS THE USA. Founding edition: WORLD IN NUMBERS carries 'OUR STANDING: HOLDING — THE RECORD BEGINS. NEXT RECKONING: 1 JAN 1955 (60 MONTHS)', the HOW THE CENTURY IS SCORED box in period prose, the six regional verdict words for both poles exactly as `compute_standings` prints them today (EUROPE: WEST DOMINATES; CENTRAL AMERICA: WEST CONTROLS; SOUTH AMERICA: WEST DOMINATES; ASIA, MIDDLE EAST: WEST PRESENT; AFRICA: NO ONE), OUTPUT as context ('INDUSTRY PER HEAD: OURS 100, THEIRS EST. 35-55'), STANDING 'NEUTRAL', PEACE 'HELD — TENSION WARY, THE TABOO INTACT'. HUD: one chip reading HOLDING, nothing else. Feb-Jun: the standing line prints every month with a cause and a panel key; the two sourced elections (Britain 23 Feb, Greece 5 Mar) cross no band and the word does not change; if the tester placed an AID program, the target's dossier PRESSURES ledger shows the flow while the provisional MAP line still reads 0, teaching that the map is slow. Late June: UNSC 83 lifts legitimacy +25 and the July line reads 'OUR STANDING: GAINING — ON LEGITIMACY ALONE [T]' (the only word change allowed in the six months; a second change is a failure). July: Korea writes the PEACE clause 'WAR IN KOREA — OUR FALLEN: 0 (EXACT)' and the intervention decision must be priced in terms: 'PROTECTS: ASIA (MAP). SPENDS: STANDING AT THE TABLE, PEACE IN MEN.' Hands-off 1955 Reckoning: MAP 0 ('THE MAP HAS NOT MOVED'), OUTPUT 0 or −1 (Soviet growth ahead in the 1950s, printed as 'THEIRS: PROBABLY FASTER (EST.)'), STANDING +1, PEACE −1 (Korea's dead) +2 (the armistice as a frozen conflict counts only if an executed treaty exists — if not, 0), era grade STALEMATE or NARROW, never CLEAR; CATASTROPHE UNSCARRED; MOVERS lists the three presence programs Moscow is running in India, Indonesia and Yugoslavia with dates so the tester knows where 1960 will be lost.

AS THE USSR. Founding edition from the party organ: 'OUR STANDING: HOLDING — THE RECORD BEGINS', the same six regional words read from the East's column (EASTERN EUROPE: BOUND; ASIA: PEKING BOUND BY TREATY, PRESENCE), OUTPUT context 'INDUSTRY PER HEAD: OURS 48 (AS REPORTED BY GOSPLAN), THEIRS EST. 90-110', STANDING 'NEUTRAL', PEACE 'HELD'. The founding box must say, in words, that non-aligned states count against Moscow as they do against Washington. Feb-Jun: the same one-change rule; the planner's own OUTPUT prints REPORTED with the AUDIT verb, and the tester must be able to find [E] ECONOMY from the line ('OUR STANDING: HOLDING — THE PLAN IS THE LEVER [E]'). July: Korea's PEACE clause reads 'WAR IN KOREA' (non-belligerent, no fallen line) and the July standing word must NOT move on the war alone. Hands-off 1955 Reckoning: MAP 0, OUTPUT ≥ 0 (momentum, gated on the economy harness), STANDING 0 or −1, PEACE 0, grade STALEMATE or NARROW; AS THEY SEE IT prints two lines from Washington's reported figures; head-to-head reads 'EVEN — WASHINGTON PROBABLY AHEAD ON STANDING' with the Kent qualifier. If the Soviet tester reads 1955 as a clear loss, the OUTPUT term or the economy calibration is wrong.

AS INDIA (one line): the founding edition reads 'OUR STANDING: HOLDING — DENIED COLUMN, ASIA. NO STANDING PROGRAMS: YOUR LEDGER MOVES ON OUTPUT AND STANDING [E] [T]', and by the 1955 freeze a hands-off India reads STALEMATE with the field holding ASIA at Presence and 'NOT YET ON THE RECORD: n BATTLEGROUNDS' under THE COLONIAL QUESTION.

Determinism acceptance: the same seed and commands print byte-identical rendered reckoning text in both apps of the determinism test at 1955-01-01, and a save loaded at 1954-12-31 reproduces the identical 1955 card.
sequencing: v1 prerequisites (same PR as the slice): extend `tuning::CHECKPOINT_YEARS` to [1955,1960,1965,1970]; seed the 1950 par in `seed` before the first command flush; add `NuclearPrograms.first_use: Option<(CountryTag,u64)>`, `Crises.prevailed/stood_down`, `Treaty.proposer` and fold them into those digests; give `LivingStandards` a `digest()` and add it to both snapshots; export `population_by_holder`; fix endgame.rs:49-50 to use `GameDate`; document that `BattlegroundDef.weight` is allocator priority, not score value.

v1 slice: `score.rs` with `Ledger`, `update_score` as the first system in `TickSet::Resolve`, `scorecards.ron` (column/reach/scale, 7 rows + default), REGION_VALUES next to thresholds in influence.ron, the four registries, the `hands_off_verdict` harness with band assertions, THE STANDING line + HUD chip, HOW THE CENTURY IS SCORED box, THE RECKONING edition with the 80-word card test, the 1970 FINAL EDITION with belief-beside-record, the one added line on the funeral screen, docs/design/systems/scoring.md at `designed` citing this research.

Economy calibration gate for OUTPUT: print both poles' five-year growth in the harness; if the planned system does not out-grow the market in 1950-60 and slow after 1963, open an economy-doc item (extensive-growth exhaustion, 1963 harvest) before the OUTPUT term is switched on; ship v1 with OUTPUT hidden behind that gate if needed.
Crush costs legitimacy in the influence mechanic (influence.rs:505-520 today charges nothing) — an influence-doc fix that the STANDING term then reads for free.

Minor-power verbs: an alignment declaration / denial treaty so the field's column stops being exogenous and MAP moves for India, Egypt, Yugoslavia; then sourced non-scoring 'THE RECORD SAYS' flavour lines for the founding edition per archetype.

Tension authorship: thread an author through every `GlobalTension::apply` (events, crisis, nuclear, settlement, war aims) — a determinism-critical cross-cutting change designed on its own — then the provocation ledger (Balance of Power 1990's Nastiness Index: RESTRAINED / FORWARD / RECKLESS) as a PEACE debit so making the AI fire first does not pay, with timeline-authored tension excluded from the player's count.

Contestability state (was an unlocked slot available when a battleground crossed against you) → the capped 'WHO LOST X?' credibility debit, only once the war system can produce a Vietnam that the cap makes cheaper than escalation.

Score-aware AI argued in the influence doc: marginal-region multiplier and pre-reckoning surge printed in the chequebook; re-bless `hands_off_anchors_land_near_history` and `hands_off_verdict` together; the AI still never reads the player's ledger.
`par_bid` per pole for difficulty and lockstep multiplayer (moves the 1950 par, never the formula), printed in the founding edition.

Multi-sponsor Great Project races (first satellite, first orbit, first thermonuclear test, the moon) with completion order as sim fact → FIRSTS on the record as legitimacy grants the STANDING term reads; until then Sputnik stays a timeline headline.
Readable bloc lock strength → a COHESION reading (great-power defection scored in the defector's region), making the Sino-Soviet split and the 1966 NATO exit visible to the map term.
Counter-cyclical write-backs once a domestic-politics/regime model exists: the trailing pole's 'do something' mandate unlocks a verb; never a capacity grant to the leader.
UNGA roll-call as a paper flavour line derived from bands once UN membership is state (Taipei's seat until 1971); never a score input.

1970 retrospective extras: DIVERGENCES column (first five OptionChosen branches / missed independence dates), 'THE WORLD WITHOUT YOU' hands-off comparison as a flourish, and a per-nation hall of records (best class per nation on the select screen).
synthesis.formula:
All integers; all inputs are existing digest-stable resources read once a month in TickSet::Resolve; the AI never reads any of it.

CONSTANTS (score::tuning unless noted)
- REGION_VALUES (data, influence.ron beside thresholds), Presence/Domination/Control: EUROPE 3/7/12, ASIA 3/7/10, MIDDLE_EAST 3/5/7, AFRICA 1/4/6, CENTRAL_AMERICA 1/3/5, SOUTH_AMERICA 2/5/6 (Twilight Struggle Deluxe 10.1, Europe Control capped at 12 instead of auto-win). None = 0. Battlegrounds count +1 each, flat (the `weight` field stays allocator priority).
- OUTPUT_STEP = 50 (permille of five-year growth per point), OUTPUT_CAP = 4.
- STANDING_STEP = 25 (legitimacy per point), STANDING_CAP = 4 (band cap; per-era delta therefore within ±3 in practice... hard cap the delta at ±3).
- PEACE_SETTLED = +2 per war you were party to that ended by an executed treaty this era, PEACE_SETTLED_CAP = +4 per era.
- PEACE_DEAD_UNIT = 2 per 10,000 of own 1950 population (−1 per unit of own dead this era), PEACE_DEAD_FLOOR = −8 per era.
- PEACE_FIRST_USE = −4 per nuclear use attributed to you this era (uncapped).
- PEACE_BRINK = −1 per month the world sat in the Brink band this era, PEACE_BRINK_FLOOR = −4, applied to the two pole leaders only.
- SCARRED_DEAD = 30 per 10,000 of own 1950 population in one era.
- Scale (scorecards.ron): superpower 1, middle 2, minor 3 (default 3, default reach = own region).
- Era grade bands on |S × scale|: STALEMATE 0-1, NARROW 2-5, CLEAR 6-11, DECISIVE 12+. Campaign class on C × scale: WON ≥ +8, HELD −7..+7, LOST ≤ −8. Monthly dead band: |provisional S × scale| ≤ 1 → HOLDING. Head-to-head dead band 2.

PER-REGION POINTS
points(r, c) = REGION_VALUES[r][verdict(count_c, max of the other two columns, thresholds_r)] + count_c, for c in {west, east, denied}; the denied column uses rival = max(west, east) so `verdict()` runs unchanged.
board(n, t) = Σ over r in reach(n) of [points(r, col(n, now)) − max over c' ≠ col of points(r, c')], with col(n, now) = the nation's live band at the freeze (Denied for NonAligned) used at BOTH ends of the delta.

STARTING VALUES (par, tick 0, seed-independent)
par.board for the West column = +41 (1955 hands-off board also +41 → MAP 0); East column −41; each nation's par is its own board(n, 1950). par.legitimacy band = 0 for everyone. par.output = actual industry per 1,000 population at tick 0 per country.

ERA TERMS (era e with previous freeze p; p = par for 1955)
- MAP(n, e) = board(n, e) − board(n, p).
- growth(n, e) = (ipc(n, e) − ipc(n, p)) × 1000 / ipc(n, p), ipc = actual_centi per 1,000 population (truth, stored; rendered through dashboard/observed helpers). comparator = growth of the other pole's leader for a bloc member; the world median growth for the field. OUTPUT(n, e) = clamp((growth(n, e) − comparator) / OUTPUT_STEP, −OUTPUT_CAP, +OUTPUT_CAP).
- legband(n, t) = clamp(legitimacy_of(n, t) / STANDING_STEP, −STANDING_CAP, +STANDING_CAP). STANDING(n, e) = clamp(legband(n, e) − legband(n, p), −3, +3).
- PEACE(n, e) = min(PEACE_SETTLED × treaties_ended(n, e), PEACE_SETTLED_CAP) + max(−floor(own_dead(n, e) × 10,000 / pop1950(n) / PEACE_DEAD_UNIT), PEACE_DEAD_FLOOR) + PEACE_FIRST_USE × uses_attributed(n, e) + (pole leaders only) max(−brink_months(e), PEACE_BRINK_FLOOR).
- S(n, e) = MAP + OUTPUT + STANDING + PEACE. Era grade word from |S × scale| with GAIN/LOSS by sign.
- Catastrophe(n, e) = EXCHANGE if GameOver exists; else SCARRED if uses_attributed(n, e) > 0 or own_dead(n, e) × 10,000 / pop1950(n) ≥ SCARRED_DEAD; else UNSCARRED.

CAMPAIGN
C(n) = S(n, 1955) + S(n, 1960) + S(n, 1965) + S(n, 1970); identity: Σ MAP = board(n, 1970) − board(n, 1950). Class = worst catastrophe state first: EXCHANGE → none for anyone; SCARRED in any era → COSTLY (printed with C's grade and the bill); UNSCARRED → WON / HELD / LOST from C × scale. Head-to-head for the poles = sign(S(USA) − S(SOV)) with dead band 2, rendered EVEN when the rival's estimate bracket exceeds the margin.

MONTHLY PROVISIONAL
Same functions against live standings, live actual output and live legitimacy since the last freeze; word = GAINING / HOLDING / SLIPPING with the dead band; cause = term with the largest |contribution| in the word's direction; arrow only after two consecutive months agreeing.

HANDS-OFF TUNING TARGETS (seed 1950, 1950-01-01 → 1970-01-01, asserted by `hands_off_verdict`; bands, never integers)
1. Neither pole's 1955 era grade is CLEAR or DECISIVE (the historian's falsifier: a clear 1955 win or loss means the weights are wrong).
2. No era for either pole is DECISIVE; both poles' campaign class is HELD.
3. Σ MAP for the East over the campaign ≥ +10 and the East holds ≥ Presence in at least three regions by 1965 (the Third World story falls out of the map; if it does not, the influence pillar, not the score, is off).
4. OUTPUT(SOV) ≥ 0 at 1955 and 1960 and ≤ 0 at 1970 — gated: if the economy sim cannot produce it, the term stays hidden and an economy calibration item is opened; the score is not re-weighted to fake it.
5. |STANDING| ≤ 1 for both poles in 1955 (the scripted UNSC 83 grant is worth at most one point).
6. Both poles UNSCARRED in every era (Korea settles without first use; hands-off dead below SCARRED_DEAD); the PRC's Korean dead read PEACE −3 and not SCARRED.
7. Every one of the 86 playable nations receives a class; a zero-slot minor's MAP is 0 in every era and its OUTPUT/STANDING are non-degenerate (at least one minor reads NARROW or better).
8. The rendered 1955 reckoning text is byte-identical across the two apps of the determinism test and after a save/load at 1954-12-31.
Knobs, in the order they may be turned: OUTPUT_STEP/CAP, STANDING_STEP, PEACE constants. REGION_VALUES and the par are never tuned to hit these targets.
